Imamatthaṃ [M 1.0124] sandhāyāti iminā kammappathappattaṃ paṭikkhipati. Attanā katañhi puññaṃ anussarato taṃ ārabbha bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavati, na pana yathā kataṃ puññaṃ sayameva pavaḍḍhati. Tasmiṃ dhamme ṭhitattāti tasmiṃ ārāmaropanādidhamme patiṭṭhitattā. Tenapi sīlena sampannattāti tena yathāvuttadhamme katasīle ṭhatvā ciṇṇena tadaññenapi kāyavācasikasaṃvaralakkhaṇena sīlena samannāgatattā. Dasa kusalā dhammā pūrenti duccaritaparivajjanato. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva.

By 'referring to this meaning,' he rejects that it has reached the course of action. For when one recollects the merit one has done, one generates much merit based on that, but the merit that was done does not increase by itself. 'Because of being established in that Dhamma' means because of being established in the Dhamma of planting parks and so on. 'Because of being endowed with that virtue as well' means because of being endowed with that virtue practiced while abiding in the aforesaid Dhamma, and also with other virtue characterized by bodily and verbal restraint. The ten wholesome qualities are fulfilled by avoiding misconduct. The rest is as has been explained.

Vanaropasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Vanaropa Sutta is concluded.

8. Jetavanasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Jetavana Sutta

48. Esitaguṇattā esiyamānaguṇattā ca isī, asekkhā sekkhakalyāṇaputhujjanā ca. Isīnaṃ saṅgho isisaṅgho. Isisaṅghena nisevitaṃ. Tenāha “bhikkhusaṅghanisevita”nti.

48. Because of seeking qualities and because of having qualities sought after, they are seers (isī)—namely, non-learners, learners, and virtuous worldlings. The community of seers is the Sangha of seers. Frequented by the Sangha of seers. Therefore, it is said, 'frequented by the Sangha of bhikkhus.'

Taṃ kārentassa gandhakuṭipāsādakūṭāgārādivasena siniddhasandacchāyarukkhalatāvasena bhūmibhāgasampattiyā ca anaññasādhāraṇaṃ atiramaṇīyaṃ taṃ jetavanaṃ cittaṃ toseti, tathā ariyānaṃ nivāsabhāvenapīti āha “evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya jetavanassa vaṇṇaṃ kathetvā”ti. Tenāha bhagavā – “yattha arahanto viharanti, taṃ bhūmirāmaṇeyyaka”nti (dha. pa. 98; theragā. 991). Apacayagāmicetanā sattānaṃ visuddhiṃ āvahati kammakkhayāya saṃvattanatoti āha “kammanti maggacetanā”ti. Catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ viditakaraṇaṭṭhena kilesānaṃ vijjhanaṭṭhena ca vijjā[V 1.0110]. Maggapaññā sammādiṭṭhīti āha “vijjāti maggapaññā”ti. Samādhipakkhikā dhammā sammāvāyāmasatisamādhayo. Yathā hi vijjāpi vijjābhāgiyā, evaṃ samādhipi samādhipakkhiko. Sīlaṃ etassa atthīti sīlanti āha “sīle patiṭṭhitassa jīvitaṃ uttama”nti. Diṭṭhisaṅkappāti sammādiṭṭhisaṅkappā. Tattha sammāsaṅkappassa sammādiṭṭhiyā upakārabhāvena vijjābhāvo vutto. Tathā hi so paññākkhandhasaṅgahitoti vuccati. Yathā ca sammāsaṅkappādayo paññākkhandhasaṅgahitā, evaṃ vāyāmasatiyo [M 1.0125] samādhikkhandhasaṅgahitāti āha “vāyāmasatisamādhayo”ti. Dhammoti hi idha samādhi adhippeto “evaṃdhammā te bhagavanto ahesu”ntiādīsu (dī. ni. 2.13; ma. ni. 3.197; saṃ. ni. 5.378) viya. Vācākammantājīvāti sammāvācākammantājīvā. Maggapariyāpannā eva hete saṅgahitā. Tenāha “etena aṭṭhaṅgikamaggenā”ti.

For the one who makes it, that Jetavana—uniquely charming due to its fragrant huts, palaces, and peaked halls, its dense and shady trees and vines, and the excellence of its terrain—pleases the mind; and also as the dwelling place of the noble ones. Thus, it is said: 'Having described the beauty of Jetavana in the first verse.' Therefore, the Blessed One declared: 'Where the arahants dwell, that land is delightful.' (Dhp 98; Thag 991). The volition that conduces to reverence brings purification to beings, leading to the exhaustion of kamma. Thus, it is said: 'Kamma means path-volition.' Knowledge (vijjā) is by way of making known the four noble truths and by way of piercing the defilements. The wisdom of the path is right view. Thus, it is said: 'Knowledge means the wisdom of the path.' The factors associated with concentration are right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. Just as knowledge is associated with knowledge factors, so too is concentration associated with concentration factors. One has virtue (sīla); thus it is said: 'For one established in virtue, life is supreme.' 'View and intention' means right view and right intention. There, right intention is said to be of the nature of knowledge because of its supportive role for right view. Indeed, it is said to be included in the aggregate of wisdom. And just as right intention and the others are included in the aggregate of wisdom, so too are effort and mindfulness included in the aggregate of concentration. Thus, it is said: 'effort, mindfulness, and concentration.' Here, 'Dhamma' means concentration, as in passages like 'Such were the Blessed Ones in their Dhamma' (DN 2.13; MN 3.197; SN 5.378). 'Speech, action, and livelihood' means right speech, right action, and right livelihood. For these are included as pertaining to the path. Therefore, it is said: 'by this eightfold path.'

Upāyena vidhinā ariyamaggo bhāvetabbo. Tenāha “samādhipakkhiyadhamma”nti. Sammāsamādhipakkhiyaṃ vipassanādhammañceva maggadhammañca. “Ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhiṃ desessāmi saupanisaṃ saparikkhāra”nti (ma. ni. 3.136) hi vacanato sammādiṭṭhiādayo maggadhammā sammāsamādhiparikkhārā. Vicineyyāti vīmaṃseyya, bhāveyyāti attho. Tatthāti hetumhi bhummavacanaṃ. Ariyamaggahetukā hi sattānaṃ visuddhi. Tenāha “tasmiṃ ariyamagge visujjhatī”ti. Pañcakkhandhadhammaṃ vicineyyāti paccuppanne pañcakkhandhe vipasseyya. Tesu vipassiyamānesu vipassanāya ukkaṃsagatāya yadaggena dukkhasaccaṃ pariññāpaṭivedhena paṭivijjhīyati, tadaggena samudayasaccaṃ pahānapaṭivedhena paṭivijjhīyati, nirodhasaccaṃ sacchikiriyāpaṭivedhena, maggasaccaṃ bhāvanāpaṭivedhena paṭivijjhīyatīti evaṃ tesu catūsu saccesu visujjhatīti imasmiṃ pakkhe nimittatthe eva bhummaṃ, tesu saccesu paṭivijjhiyamānesūti attho.

The noble path should be developed by means and method. Therefore, it is said: 'the factors pertaining to concentration.' The factors pertaining to right concentration include both insight-related phenomena and path-related phenomena. For it is said, 'Monks, I will teach you noble right concentration with its supports and requisites' (MN 3.136); thus, right view and other path factors are the requisites of right concentration. 'One should investigate' means one should examine; 'one should develop' is the meaning. 'In that' is a locative expression indicating cause. For the purification of beings is caused by the noble path. Therefore, it is said: 'in that noble path, one is purified.' 'One should investigate the phenomena of the five aggregates' means one should contemplate the presently arisen five aggregates with insight. When these are contemplated with insight, as insight becomes heightened, then with the culmination of insight, the truth of suffering is penetrated through the penetration of full understanding; the truth of the origin is penetrated through the penetration of abandoning; the truth of cessation is penetrated through the penetration of realization; and the truth of the path is penetrated through the penetration of development. Thus, one is purified in these four truths. In this context, the locative case indicates the object, meaning, 'while penetrating those truths.'

Avadhāraṇavacananti vavatthāpanavacanaṃ, avadhāraṇanti attho. “Sāriputtovā”ti ca avadhāraṇaṃ sāvakesu sāriputtova seyyoti imamatthaṃ dīpeti tassevukkaṃsabhāvato. Kilesaupasamenāti iminā mahātherassa tādiso kilesavūpasamoti dasseti. Tassa sāvakavisaye paññāya pāramippatti ahosi. Yadi evaṃ “yopi pāraṅgato bhikkhu, etāvaparamo siyā”ti idaṃ tesaṃ buddhānaṃ ñāṇavisaye paññāpāramippattānaṃ vaseneva vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Avadhāraṇampi vimuttiyā nānattā tīhi vimuttīhi pāraṅgate sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenāha – “pāraṃ gatoti nibbānaṃ [V 1.0111] gato”tiādi. Na therena uttaritaro nāma atthi labbhati, labbhati ce, evameva labbheyyāti adhippāyo.

'A statement of emphasis' (avadhāraṇavacana) means a statement of specification (vavatthāpanavacana); 'emphasis' (avadhāraṇa) is the meaning. And 'Sāriputta alone' is also an emphasis, indicating the meaning that Sāriputta alone is supreme among disciples, due to his excellence. 'By the pacification of defilements' shows that the great elder had such a pacification of defilements. His attainment of the perfection of wisdom was in the sphere of disciples. If so, it should be understood that this statement, 'even a monk who has gone beyond, this would be his highest,' was spoken with reference to those who have attained the perfection of wisdom in the sphere of the knowledge of those Buddhas. The emphasis also, due to the diversity of liberation, was spoken with reference to one who has gone beyond by the three liberations. Therefore, it is said: 'gone beyond means gone to Nibbāna,' etc. No one greater than the elder can be found; if one could be found, one would be found just like him—this is the intention.

Jetavanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Jetavana Sutta is concluded.

9. Maccharisuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Macchari Sutta.

49. Maccharinoti [M 1.0126] maccheravanto maccherasamaṅginoti āha “maccherena samannāgatā”ti. Maccheraṃ macchariyanti atthato ekaṃ. Na vandatīti vandanamattampi na karoti, kuto dānanti adhippāyo. Upaṭṭhānaṃ kātunti madhurapaṭisanthāraṃ karotīti yojanā. Idaṃ tāva mudumacchariyaṃ na hadayaṃ viya attānaṃ dassentassa macchariyanti katvā. Kiṃ tuyhaṃ pādā rujjanti nanu tuyhaṃyeva āgatagamanesu pādā rujjanti, kinte ime chindantīti adhippāyo. Sāmīcimpi na karoti kuto dānanti adhippāyo. Yathākammaṃ taṃtaṃgatiyo aranti upagacchantīti ariyā, sattā. Ime pana kucchitā ariyāti kadariyā, thaddhamaccharino. Macchariyasadisañhi kucchitaṃ sabbahīnaṃ natthi sabbaguṇābhibhūtattā bhogasampattiādisabbasampattīnaṃ mūlabhūtassa dānassa nisedhato. Itiādīhi vacanehi. Attano upaghātakoti macchariyānuyogena kusaladhammānaṃ gatisampattiyā ca vināsako.

49. 'Miserly' (maccharī) means one who is full of miserliness, associated with miserliness; thus it is said, 'endowed with miserliness.' Miserliness (macchera) and stinginess (macchariya) are the same in meaning. 'He does not bow' means he does not perform even the gesture of bowing, let alone giving—this is the intent. 'To provide service' is to be connected with 'to offer warm hospitality.' This, for now, is mild miserliness, not the miserliness of one who shows himself as if showing his own heart. 'Why, do your feet hurt? Surely, it is only your own feet that hurt from coming and going. Why do they cut these for you?'—this is the intent. 'He does not even do what is proper,' let alone giving—this is the intent. Because beings (sattā) go (aranti) to their respective destinations according to their kamma, they are called noble ones (ariyā). But these contemptible noble ones (kucchitā ariyā) are the stingy (kadariyā), the hard-hearted misers. For there is nothing as despicable and utterly base as miserliness—as it overpowers all good qualities and obstructs generosity, which is the root of all prosperity, such as wealth and other attainments—and so on with other such words. 'A destroyer of oneself' means one who, by indulging in miserliness, destroys wholesome qualities and the attainment of a good rebirth.

Puññapāpavasena samparetabbato upagantabbato samparāyo, paraloko. Kāmaguṇaratīti kāmaguṇasannissayo assādo. Khiḍḍāti kāyikakhiḍḍā vācasikakhiḍḍā cetasikakhiḍḍāti evaṃ tividhā. Esa vipākoti coḷādīnaṃ kicchalābhoti esa evarūpo vipāko. Yamalokanti paralokaṃ. Upapajjareti ettha iti-saddo pakārattho. Tena pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ nirayaṃ tiracchānayoniñca saṅgaṇhāti.

The next world (samparāyo) is so called because it is to be approached or entered based on merit and demerit; it is the other world (paraloko). 'Delighting in the qualities of sensual pleasure' (kāmaguṇaratī) means the enjoyment of, or reliance on, the qualities of sensual pleasure. 'Play' (khiḍḍā) is of three kinds: bodily play, verbal play, and mental play. 'This is the result' (esa vipāko) means such a result as obtaining robes and so on with difficulty. 'The world of Yama' (yamaloka) means the other world. In 'upapajjare'ti', the word 'iti' has the sense of 'kind.' Therefore, it includes hell and the animal realm, which are mentioned in the Pāli text.

Yācanti nāma ariyayācanāya. Vuttañhetaṃ “uddissa ariyā tiṭṭhanti, esā ariyāna yācanā”ti (jā. 1.7.59). Ye saṃvibhajanti, te vadaññū nāma ñatvā kattabbakaraṇato. Vimānappabhāyāti nidassanamattaṃ, uyyānakapparukkhappabhāhi devatānaṃ vatthābharaṇasarīrappabhāhipi sagge pakāsentiyeva. Pakāsantīti vā pākaṭā honti, na apāyaloke viya apākaṭāti attho. Parasambhatesūti sayaṃ sambhataṃ anāpajjitvā pareheva sambharitesu sukhūpakaraṇesu. Tenāha pāḷiyaṃ “vasavattīva modare”ti, paranimmitabhogesu vasavattī devaputtā viya sukhasamaṅgitāya modantīti attho. Evaṃ vuttasamparāyoti ete saggāti evaṃ heṭṭhā [M 1.0127] vuttasamparāyo. Ubhinnanti etesaṃ yathāvuttānaṃ ubhinnaṃ dukkaṭasukaṭakammakārīnaṃ. Tato cavitvā tato nirayasaggādito cavitvā [V 1.0112] manussesu nibbattati. Tesu yo maccharī manussesu nibbatto, so daliddo hutvā pubbacariyavasena maccharīyeva honto dārādibharaṇatthaṃ macchakacchapādīni hantvā punapi niraye nibbatto. Itaro suddhāsayo samiddho hutvā pubbacariyāvasena punapi puññāni katvā sagge nibbatteyya. Tenāha “puna samparāyepi duggatisugatiyeva hotī”ti.

‘They ask’ (yācanti) refers to the noble request. For it is said: ‘For the sake of the noble ones they stand, this is the request of the noble ones’ (Jā. 1.7.59). Those who share (saṃvibhajanti) are called generous (vadaññū), because they know what should be done and do it. ‘Shining like a celestial mansion’ (vimānappabhāya) is merely illustrative; in heaven, the radiance of gardens, wish-fulfilling trees, and the bodies, garments, and ornaments of deities also shines brightly. Or, ‘they shine’ (pakāsanti) means they are manifest, not unmanifest like in the woeful world—this is the meaning. ‘With others’ provisions’ (parasambhatesu) means with provisions gathered by others, without having acquired them oneself, which are conducive to happiness. Therefore, the Pāli text says, ‘they rejoice like Vasavattī’ (vasavattīva modare), meaning they rejoice in happiness like the Vasavattī devas who enjoy what others have created. ‘Thus, the hereafter is spoken of’ (evaṃ vuttasamparāyo) refers to these heavens, meaning the hereafter mentioned previously. ‘Of both’ (ubhinnaṃ) refers to these two types of beings, those who perform both bad and good deeds, as mentioned before. Having passed away from there—from hell or heaven—one is reborn among humans. Among them, the miserly one reborn as a human becomes poor and, due to past conduct, remains miserly, even killing fish, turtles, etc., to support his family, and is reborn again in hell. The other, being pure-minded and prosperous, due to past conduct, again performs meritorious deeds and is reborn in heaven. Therefore, it is said: ‘Again, in the next life, there is either a woeful or a blissful destination’ (puna samparāyepi duggatisugatiyeva hoti).

Maccharisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Macchari Sutta is concluded.

10. Ghaṭīkārasuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Ghaṭīkāra Sutta

50. “Upapannāse”ti se-kārāgamaṃ katvā niddeso, “upapannā”icceva atthoti āha “nibbattivasena upagatā”ti. Attano sampattito avihānato avihā, tesaṃ brahmaloko avihābrahmaloko, tasmiṃ. Upapattisamanantaramevāti paṭhamakoṭṭhāse eva. Arahattaphalavimuttiyāti asekkhavimuttiyā. Sekkhavimuttiyā pana avihūpapattito pageva vimuttā. Mānusaṃ dehaṃ samatikkamanti cittupakkilesapahānavasenāti phalena hetudassanamidanti āha “mānusaṃ dehanti idha…pe… vuttānī”ti. Divi bhavaṃ dibbaṃ, brahmattabhāvasaññitaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ. Tattha saṃyojanakoti vuttaṃ “dibbaṃ yoganti pañca uddhambhāgiyasaṃyojanānī”ti. Imassāti devaputtassa. “Hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccagu”nti tesaṃ tvaṃ kusalaṃ sabbāvajjappahānena anavajjataṃ bhāsatīti kusalī vadesi. Atthena saddassa abhedopacāraṃ katvā gambhīravacanaṃ vuttanti āha “gambhīrattha”nti atthasseva gambhīrato, na saddassa. Samucchinnakāmarāgatāya sabbaso kāmavisayappahānena nirāmisabrahmacārī nāma anāgāmī. Nivāsanaṭṭhānabhūto samāno eko gāmo etassāti āha “ekagāmavāsī”ti.

50. ‘Upapannāse’ is a designation made by adding the augment ‘se’; the meaning is simply ‘upapannā,’ as it is said, ‘having come into existence by way of rebirth.’ ‘Avihā’ means not departing from one’s own attainment; their Brahma world is the Avihā Brahma world, therein. ‘Immediately upon rebirth’ (upapattisamanantarameva) means right in the first division. ‘By the liberation of the fruit of Arahantship’ (arahattaphalavimuttiyā) refers to the liberation of the non-trainee. As for the liberation of the trainee, they are liberated even before rebirth in Avihā. ‘They transcend the human body’ (mānusaṃ dehaṃ samatikkamanti) by way of abandoning mental defilements—this is showing the cause through the fruit, hence it is said, ‘the human body here… as stated.’ That which exists in the divine realm is divine (dibbaṃ), meaning the five aggregates designated as the state of Brahma. There, what is called ‘the divine yoke’ (dibbaṃ yogaṃ) refers to the five higher fetters. ‘Of this’ (imassa) refers to the young deva. ‘Having abandoned the human body, they have gone beyond the divine yoke’ (hitvā mānusaṃ dehaṃ, dibbayogaṃ upaccaguṃ)—you speak of their goodness, their blamelessness through the abandonment of all faults; thus you speak skillfully (kusalī). By treating the meaning and the word without distinction, profound speech is spoken—hence ‘profound meaning’ (gambhīratthaṃ), meaning profound in meaning, not in word. One who has completely cut off sensual desire, entirely abandoning the realm of sensuality, is called a non-returner (anāgāmī), a spiritual practitioner free from sensual pleasures (nirāmisa-brahmacārī). ‘Dweller in a single village’ (ekagāmavāsī) is said because a single village is his dwelling place.

Ghaṭīkārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Ghaṭīkāra Sutta is concluded.

Ādittavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Āditta Vagga is concluded.

6. Jarāvaggo

6. The Chapter on Old Age

1. Jarāsuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Discourse on Old Age

51. Hitassa [M 1.0128] sādhanato sādhu, yaṃ kiñci atthajātaṃ. Taṃ pana atthakāmena labhitabbato upasevitabbato [V 1.0113] laddhakaṃ, kalyāṇaṭṭhena bhaddakanti vuccatīti āha “sādhūti laddhakaṃ bhaddaka”nti. “Sīlaṃ yāva jarā sādhū”ti vuttamatthaṃ byatirekato vibhāvetuṃ “iminā idaṃ dassetī”ti vuttaṃ. Idanti idaṃ atthajātaṃ.

51. ‘Good’ (sādhu) is so called because it accomplishes benefit (hita), whatever kind of benefit it may be. But since it is to be acquired and cultivated by one who desires benefit, it is ‘acquired’ (laddhakaṃ), and is called ‘auspicious’ (bhaddakaṃ) in the sense of being wholesome (kalyāṇa). Hence, it is said: ‘“Good” means what is acquired, what is auspicious.’ To explain the meaning stated, ‘virtue is good until old age,’ by way of contrast, it is said: ‘By this, this is shown.’ ‘This’ (idaṃ) refers to this kind of benefit.

Patiṭṭhitāti cittasantāne laddhapatiṭṭhā, kenaci asaṃhāriyā. Tenāha “maggena āgatā”ti. Cittīkataṭṭhādīhīti pūjanīyabhāvādīhi. Vuttaṃ hetaṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Cittīkatanti ratananti idaṃ ratanaṃ nāma loke cittīkataṃ vatthūnaṃ sahassagghanatādivasena. Yepi loke cittīkatā khattiyapaṇḍita-catumahārāja-sakka-suyāma-mahābrahmādayo, tesaṃ cittīkato tehi saraṇanti upagantabbatādivasena. Ratikaranti pītisukhāvahaṃ. Jhānaratisukhenāti duvidhenapi jhānaratisukhena. Tuletunti paricchindituṃ. Guṇapāraminti guṇānaṃ ukkaṃsapāramiṃ. Dullabho anekāni asaṅkhyeyyāni atidhāvitvāpi laddhuṃ asakkuṇeyyattā. Anomoti anūno paripuṇṇo. Tattha visesato anomasattaparibhogato tehi “sammāsambuddho bhagavā”ti anussaritabbatoti āha “bhagavā anomo sīlenā”tiādi.

“Established” (patiṭṭhitā) means having gained a firm footing in the mind-continuum, unshaken by anything. Hence it is said: “arrived by the path.” “Being made precious” (cittīkataṭṭhādīhi) refers to being worthy of veneration and so on. This is stated in the ancient commentary. “Made precious” (cittīkataṃ) means this jewel, in the world, is highly valued, like material things worth thousands. Even those esteemed in the world—kings, scholars, the Four Great Kings, Sakka, Suyāma, Mahābrahmā, and others—venerate it, as it is worthy of being gone to for refuge and so on. “Delighting” (ratikaraṃ) means bringing joy and happiness. “With the joy and happiness of jhāna” (jhānaratisukhena) refers to the twofold joy and happiness of jhāna. “To measure” (tuletuṃ) means to delimit. “The summit of virtues” (guṇapāramiṃ) is the unsurpassed excellence of virtues. “Rare” (dullabho) because even after running through many incalculable aeons, it is impossible to obtain. “Peerless” (anomo) means not inferior, complete. Here, particularly because it is enjoyed by the peerless being, it should be recollected by them thus: ‘The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One.’ Hence it is said: ‘The Blessed One is peerless in virtue,’ etc.

Ariyamaggapaññāyeva idha adhippetāti “idha pana dullabhapātubhāvaṭṭhena paññā ‘ratana’nti vutta”nti āha. Pujjaphalanibbattanato, attano santānaṃ punātīti ca puññacetanā puññaṃ, sā pana yassa uppannā, tasseva āveṇikatāya anaññasādhāraṇattā kenacipi anāhaṭā, aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “arūpattā”ti vuttaṃ.

Here, wisdom regarding the Noble Path is specifically intended. Thus, it is said: “Here, due to the difficulty of its arising, wisdom is called ‘jewel.’” Because it produces the fruit of veneration, and because the intention of merit (puññacetanā) purifies one’s own continuum, that intention is merit. But that which has arisen in someone is unique to them, not shared by others; it is unassailable by anyone. In the commentary, however, it is said: “because it is formless.”

Jarāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Old Age is concluded.

2. Ajarasāsuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Discourse on Non-Decay

52. Ajīraṇenāti [M 1.0129] jiṇṇabhāvānāpajjanena. Lakkhaṇavacanañcetaṃ avināsappattiyā. Tenāha “avipattiyāti attho”ti. Niddhamitabboti nīharitabbo.

52. “By not decaying” (ajīraṇena) means by not reaching a state of decay. And this is a characteristic designation of attaining non-destruction. Hence it is said: “the meaning is non-ruin.” “Should be expelled” (niddhamitabbo) means should be taken out.

Ajarasāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on Non-Decay is concluded.

3. Mittasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Discourse on a Friend

53. Saha atthena vattatīti sattho, bhaṇḍamūlaṃ gahetvā vāṇijjavasena desantarādīsu vicaraṇakajanasamūho. Tenāha “saddhiṃcaro”ti, sahacaraṇakoti attho. Mittanti sinehayogena mittakiccayuttaṃ[V 1.0114]. Idhādhippetappakāraṃ dassetuṃ “roge uppanne”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tathārūpeti jigucchanīye, duttikicche vā. Yathā asaṇṭhitānaṃ saṇṭhāpanavasena pavasato purisassa bhogabyasane nāthatā, evaṃ puttasinehavasena puttassa mātuyā antogehe nāthatāti vuttaṃ “mātā mittaṃ sake ghare”ti. Atthajātassāti upaṭṭhitapayojanassāti atthoti āha “uppannakiccassā”ti. Samparāyahitanti samparāye hitāvahaṃ.

53. Because it proceeds with goods (attha), it is called a caravan (sattha), a group of people traveling together for trade, carrying goods and capital, journeying to distant lands. Hence it is said: ‘a fellow traveler’ (saddhiṃcaro), meaning one who accompanies. A friend (mitta) is one connected by affection and endowed with the duties of friendship. Here, to illustrate the intended meaning, it is said: ‘when illness arises,’ and so on. ‘In such a case’ (tathārūpe) refers to what is repulsive or difficult to care for. Just as a man who has gone abroad to establish the unsettled is a protector in the misfortune of wealth, so too is a mother a protector in her own home due to affection for her son—as stated: ‘a mother is a friend in her own home.’ ‘Of one for whom a need has arisen’ (atthajātassa) means one with a present purpose; thus it is said: ‘one with an arisen task.’ ‘Beneficial for the hereafter’ (samparāyahitaṃ) means bringing welfare in the future.

Mittasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on a Friend is concluded.

4. Vatthusuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Discourse on the Basis

54. Patiṭṭhāti avassayo. Guyhassāti guhitabbassa rahassassa. Paramo sakhā nāma atipiyaṭṭhānatāya.

54. ‘A foundation’ (patiṭṭhā) means a support. ‘Of a secret’ (guyhassa) means of that which should be concealed, that which is private. ‘A supreme friend’ (paramo sakhā) is so called because of being extremely dear.

Vatthusuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Basis is concluded.

5. Paṭhamajanasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the First Discourse on a Person

55. Vidhāvatīti vividhaṃ rūpaṃ padhāvati, yathākāmaṃ pavattatīti attho.

55. “Runs about” (vidhāvati) means it runs to various forms, proceeding as it pleases—this is the meaning.

Paṭhamajanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the First Discourse on a Person is concluded.

6. Dutiyajanasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Second Discourse on a Person

56. Vaṭṭadukkhatoti [M 1.0130] saṃsāradukkhato. Saṃsāro hi kilesakammavipākānaṃ aparāparuppattitāya vidhāvati. Tañca dukkhaṃ dukkhamattāya nānāvidhadukkharāsibhāvato.

56. “From the suffering of the round” (vaṭṭadukkhato) means from the suffering of saṃsāra. For saṃsāra rushes on because of the successive arising of defilements, kamma, and their results. And that is suffering because it is suffering in itself, and because it is a mass of various kinds of suffering.

Dutiyajanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Discourse on a Person is concluded.

7. Tatiyajanasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Third Discourse on a Person

57. Nipphattīti iṭṭhāniṭṭhavipākānaṃ nipphajjanato nipphatti. Tato eva avassayo, nipphattitavipākassa avassayo adhiṭṭhānaṃ kāraṇanti attho.

57. “Production” (nipphatti) is so called because of the production (nipphajjanato) of desirable and undesirable results. For that very reason, it is a support—the support for the produced result, meaning the basis or cause.

Tatiyajanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Third Discourse on a Person is concluded.

8. Uppathasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Discourse on the Wrong Path

58. Amaggoti [V 1.0115] na maggo anupāyo. Rattindivakkhayoti tattha vayakkhaṇassa pākaṭabhāvato. Vuttakkhaṇopi hi sayaṃ khīyateva. Sesaṃ bāhiramalaṃ vatthasarīrādibhūtaṃ. Tathā hi “bhasmakhārādīhi dhovitvā sakkā sodhetu”nti vuttaṃ. Duṭṭhoti dūsito sattasantāno na sakkā suddho nāma kātuṃ abbhantaramalīnabhāvāpādanato. Itthiyanti brahmacariyassa antarāyakarāyapi. Pajāti sattakāyo sajjati saṅgaṃ karoti yāthāvato ādīnavaṃ apassanto. Indriyasaṃvarādi kilesānaṃ tāpanato tapo, tenāha “sabbāpī”tiādi.

58. “Not the path” (amaggo) means it is not the path, it is without means. “The destruction of day and night” (rattindivakkhayo) refers to the evident nature of decay there. For even the past moment itself perishes. The rest is external impurity, pertaining to things like cloth, the body, etc. Thus, it is said: “It can be cleansed by washing with ashes, lye, and the like.” “Corrupt” (duṭṭho) means defiled; the continuum of a being cannot be made pure, due to its bringing about an inner state of impurity. The term 'woman' (itthiyaṃ) is used because she is an obstacle to the holy life. “The multitude” (pajā) refers to the group of beings, who cling, forming attachments, not seeing the inherent dangers as they actually are. “Austerity” (tapo) is the torment of defilements through restraint of the senses, etc.; therefore, it is said: “All these…”

Uppathasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Wrong Path is concluded.

9. Dutiyasuttavaṇṇanā

9. The Commentary on the Second Sutta

59. Kissāti [M 1.0131] bhummatthe sāmivacananti āha “kismiṃ abhirato”ti. Saddhā nāma anavajjasabhāvā, tasmā lokiyalokuttarahitasukhāvahāti āha “sugatiñceva nibbānañca gacchantassa dutiyikā”ti. Anusāsati hitacariyāya pariṇāyikabhāvato.

59. ‘Kissā’ is a genitive, which implies ownership, used here in the sense of the locative; thus he says, ‘In what does one delight?’ ‘Faith’ (saddhā) is so called because its nature is blameless; therefore, since it brings happiness and welfare, both worldly and supramundane, he says, ‘a companion for one going to a good destination and Nibbāna.’ ‘Admonishes’ (anusāsati) means it is a leader directing towards beneficial conduct.

Dutiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Sutta is concluded.

10. Kavisuttavaṇṇanā

10. The Commentary on the Kavi Sutta

60. Gāyattiādikoti chabbīsatiyā chandesu gāyattiādiko ukkatipariyosāno chando gāthānaṃ nidānaṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ “samuṭṭhahati etenā”ti katvā. Tehi pana anuṭṭhubhādiko hotīti āha “chando gāthānaṃ nidāna”nti. Pubbapaṭṭhāpanagāthāti dhammakathāya ādito ārocanabhāvajānanatthaṃ satijananaṃ viya pavattitagāthā. Akkharañhi padaṃ janetīti yasmā akkharasamudāyo padaṃ, padasamudāyo gāthā, samudāyo ca samudāyīhi byañjīyati taṃpavattanato, tasmā byañjanabhāve ṭhitaṃ akkharaṃ, taṃsamudāyo padaṃ, padaṃ taṃ viyañjetā janetā viya hotīti “akkharañhi padaṃ janetī”ti vuttaṃ. Akkharaṃ hi uccāritaviddhaṃsitāya taṃtaṃkhaṇamattāvaṭṭhāyīpi parato pavattiyā manoviññāṇavīthiyā saṅkalanavasena ekajjhaṃ katvā padabhāvena gayhamānaṃ yathāsaṅketamatthaṃ byañjeti. Padaṃ gāthaṃ janetīti etthāpi eseva nayo. Gāthā atthaṃ pakāsetīti gāthāsaññito padasamudāyo kiriyākārakasambandhavasena sambandhito kattuadhippāyānurūpaṃ ālocitavilocitaṃ saṃhitaṃ atthaṃ vibhāveti. Samuddādipaṇṇattinissitā vohārasannissayeneva [V 1.0116] pavattatīti katvā. Tenāha “gāthā ārabhanto”tiādi. Āsayoti avassayoti āha “patiṭṭhā”ti kavitoti vicittakathīādito.

60. ‘Gāyattiādiko’ means that among the twenty-six meters, the meter beginning with Gāyattī and ending with Ukkatī is the origin and source of verses, because it is said, ‘It arises from this.’ And since from these the Anuṭṭhubha and other meters arise, he says, ‘The meter is the origin of verses.’ ‘Introductory verse’ (pubbapaṭṭhāpanagāthā) refers to a verse recited at the beginning of a Dhamma talk, as if generating mindfulness, for the purpose of announcing and making known the subject. For it is said, ‘Letters indeed produce a word.’ Because a collection of letters forms a word, and a collection of words forms a verse, and a collection is manifested by its components through their operation, therefore a letter, existing in the state of being a manifesting entity, and a collection of those, i.e., a word, produces it, becoming like a manifester. Thus it is said, ‘Letters indeed produce a word.’ A letter, though existing only for a moment when uttered and dissolved, when combined through recollection in the course of the mental consciousness process and grasped as a word, expresses meaning according to convention. Similarly, regarding ‘a word produces a verse,’ the same principle applies here. ‘The verse clarifies the meaning’ means that the collection of words recognized as a verse, being connected through action-agent relationships, reveals a coherent meaning, examined and analyzed, in accordance with the speaker’s intention. Because it operates based on conventional usage, which relies on concepts such as 'ocean', therefore, he says, ‘One who begins a verse,’ and so on. ‘Āsayo’ means ‘support,’ thus he says, ‘foundation.’ ‘Kavi’ refers to a skilled speaker with elaborate speech, and so on.

Kavisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kavi Sutta is concluded.

Jarāvaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Old Age is concluded.

7. Addhavaggo

7. The Chapter on Time

1. Nāmasuttavaṇṇanā

1. The Commentary on the Nāma Sutta

61. Nāmanti [M 1.0132] sāmaññanāmādibhedaṃ nāmaṃ. Sabbanti sabbaṃ paññattipathaṃ sabbaṃ ñeyyapavattipathaṃ. Addhabhavīti kāmaṃ pāḷiyaṃ atītakālaniddeso kato, taṃ pana lakkhaṇamattaṃ. Abhibhavati anupatatīti etena abhibhavo anupatanaṃ pavatti evāti dasseti. Taṃ panassa abhibhavanaṃ appavisaye anāmasitvā mahāvisayānaṃ vasena dassento “opapātikena vā”tiādimāha. Tassa nāmaṃ hotīti tassa rukkhapāsāṇādikassa anāmakoicceva samaññā hoti, tathā naṃ sañjānantīti attho.

61. ‘Nāma’ (name) refers to name as distinguished into general name and so on. ‘Sabba’ (all) means all that is within the scope of concepts, all that is within the scope of knowable processes. Regarding ‘addhabhavī’ (it has overcome), although the past tense is used in the Pāli, that is merely an indication of a characteristic. By ‘abhibhavati’ (it overcomes) and ‘anupatati’ (it pursues), he shows that overcoming is a pursuit, is process itself. But showing its overcoming by way of great domains, without referring to insignificant domains, he said, ‘by spontaneous rebirth,’ and so on. ‘That is its name’ means that for that tree, rock, and so on, it is indeed nameless, it is only a designation; thus, they recognize it as such—this is the meaning.

Nāmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Nāma Sutta is concluded.

2. Cittasuttavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Citta Sutta

62. Ye cittassa vasaṃ gacchantīti ye apariññātavatthukā, tesaṃyeva. Anavasesapariyādānanti anavasesaggahaṇaṃ. Na hi pariññātakkhandhā pahīnakilesā cittassa vasaṃ gacchanti, taṃ attano vase vattenti.

62. ‘Those who come under the sway of the mind’ refers to those whose objects are not fully comprehended, and to them alone. ‘Complete mastery’ (anavasesapariyādāna) means complete grasping. For those who have fully understood the aggregates and abandoned the defilements do not come under the sway of the mind; rather, they keep it under their own control.

Cittasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Citta Sutta is concluded.

3. Taṇhāsuttavaṇṇanā

3. The Commentary on the Taṇhā Sutta

63. Tatiye [V 1.0117] “sabbeva vasamanvagū”ti ye taṇhāya vasaṃ gacchanti, tesaṃ eva anavasesapariyādānanti imamatthaṃ “eseva nayo”ti iminā atidissati.

63. In the third sutta, by the phrase ‘this is the same method,’ this meaning is indicated: that ‘all indeed come under its sway’ refers to the complete mastery, without remainder, over those who come under the sway of craving.

Taṇhāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Taṇhā Sutta is concluded.

4. Saṃyojanasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Saṃyojana Sutta

64. Kiṃ [M 1.0133] su saṃyojanoti sūti nipātamattanti āha “kiṃ-saṃyojano”ti? Vicaranti etehīti vicāraṇā, pādā. Bahuvacane hi vattabbe ekavacanaṃ kataṃ. Tassāti lokassa.

64. Regarding ‘Kiṃ su saṃyojano’ (What is a fetter?), he says that ‘su’ is merely a particle, thus he asks ‘Kiṃ-saṃyojano?’ (What fetter?). ‘Vicāraṇā’ (wandering) means ‘they wander by these,’ referring to the feet. Although the plural should be used, the singular is employed. ‘Tassa’ (of this) refers to the world.

Saṃyojanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Saṃyojana Sutta is concluded.

5. Bandhanasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Bandhana Sutta

65. Catutthe āgataattho eva anantarepi vutto, byañjanameva nānanti āha “pañcamepi eseva nayo”ti.

65. The meaning presented in the fourth sutta is the same as that stated in the one immediately preceding it; only the phrasing is different. Thus he says, ‘In the fifth sutta too, this is the same method.’

Bandhanasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bandhana Sutta is concluded.

6. Attahatasuttavaṇṇanā

6. The Commentary on the Attahata Sutta

66. “Kenassubbhāhato”ti pāṭhoti adhippāyena “su-kāro nipātamatta”nti āha, “kenassabbhāhato”ti pana pāṭhe u-kāralopena padasandhi. Icchādhūpāyitoti asampattavisayicchālakkhaṇāya taṇhāya santāpito daḍḍho. Tenāha “icchāya āditto”ti.

66. Regarding the reading ‘Kenassubbhāhato’ (By what is one utterly struck?), he says that according to the intended meaning, the ‘su’ is merely a particle. But in the reading ‘kenassabbhāhato,’ the vowel ‘u’ is elided as a euphonic combination. ‘Scorched by the smoke of desire’ (icchādhūpāyito) means burned by craving, which has the characteristic of desiring unobtained objects. Thus he said, ‘set aflame by desire.’

Attahatasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Attahata Sutta is concluded.

7. Uḍḍitasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Explanation of the Uḍḍita Sutta

67. Ullaṅghitoti ubbandhitvā laṅghito. Saddādīsūti saddādināgadantesu sotādīni uḍḍitāni taṇhārajjunā daḷhabandhanena baddhattā tadanativattanato. Lokoti āyatanaloko. Tathā atthayojanāya katattā khandhādilokavasenapi yojanā kātabbā. Na dūraṃ [M 1.0134] anantarabhavakattā. Cuticittaantaritattā [V 1.0118] ekacittantarabhavassa kammassa abujjhanaṃ, evaṃ sante kasmā sattā na bujjhantīti āha “balavatiyā”tiādi.

67. "Leapt over" (ullaṅghito) means "having tied up, it is flung." "By sounds, etc." (saddādīsu): The ears and other sense organs are hoisted on the pegs of sound and so forth, bound by the strong bond of the rope of craving, so that they cannot transcend them. "The world" (loko) refers to the world of the sense bases. Similarly, for the purpose of application, an application should also be made in terms of the world of aggregates, etc. "Not far" (na dūraṃ) means "as the creator of the immediately subsequent existence." Since it is separated by the death-consciousness, there is no awakening to the kamma of the existence with a one-mind-moment interval. This being so, why do beings not awaken? He said, "because of its great strength," etc.

Uḍḍitasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Uḍḍita Sutta is finished.

8. Pihitasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Pihita Sutta

68. Pañhoti ñātuṃ icchito attho. Pucchitoti sattamasutte gāthāya purimaddhaṃ pacchimaddhaṃ, pacchimaṃ purimaṃ katvā aṭṭhamasutte devatāya pucchitattā vuttaṃ “heṭṭhupariyāyavasena pucchito”ti. Pucchānurūpaṃ vissajjananti avuttampi siddhametanti anāhaṭaṃ.

68. "Question" (pañho) means "the meaning desired to be known." Regarding "asked" (pucchito): because in the eighth sutta it was asked by a deity, with the first half of the verse from the seventh sutta made the second half, and the second half made the first, it is said, "asked in reverse order." The reply is in accordance with the question—this is established even if unstated; therefore, it is not brought up.

Pihitasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Pihita Sutta is finished.

9. Icchāsuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Icchā Sutta

69. Navame vinayāyāti vinayena. Karaṇatthe hi idaṃ sampadānavacanaṃ. Kissassūti kissa, su-kāro nipātamattaṃ. Sabbaṃ chindati bandhananti sabbaṃ dasavidhampi saṃyojanaṃ samucchindati. Na hi taṃ kiñci kilesabandhanaṃ atthi, yaṃ asamucchinnaṃ hutvā ṭhitaṃ assā taṇhāya samucchinnāya. Svāyamattho suviññeyyoti āha “sabbaṃ uttānamevā”ti.

69. In the ninth, "for the sake of discipline" (vinayāya) means "by means of discipline" (vinayena). This dative case is used in the sense of the instrumental. "Of what?" (kissassu) means "of what?" (kissa); the particle "su" is merely emphatic. "He cuts all bonds" (sabbaṃ chindati bandhanaṃ) means "he completely severs all ten fetters." For there is no bond of defilement that remains uncut when craving is cut off. This meaning is easily understood—hence it is said, "all is evident."

Icchāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Icchā Sutta is finished.

10. Lokasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Loka Sutta

70. Kisminti kismiṃ sati? Tassa pana santabhāvo uppattivasenevāti āha “kismiṃ uppanne”ti? Loko uppannoti vuccati anupādānattā lokasamaññāya. Chasūti etthāpi eseva nayo santhavanti adhikasinehaṃ [M 1.0135] karoti adhikasinehavatthubhāvato ajjhattikāyatanānaṃ. Upādāyāti pubbakālakiriyā aparakālakiriyaṃ apekkhatīti vacanasesavasena kiriyāpadaṃ gahitaṃ “pavattatī”ti. Kiṃ pana pavattati? Loko, lokasamaññāti attho. Chasūti idaṃ nimittatthe bhummaṃ. Chaḷāyatananimittañhi sabbadukkhaṃ. Ayanti sattaloko. Uppanno nāma hoti chaḷāyatanaṃ nāma mūlaṃ sabbadukkhānanti katvā. Bāhiresu āyatanesu santhavaṃ karoti visesato rūpādīnaṃ taṇhāvatthukattā. Yasmā cakkhādīnaṃ santappanavasena [V 1.0119] rūpādīnaṃ pariggahitattā lokassa nisevitāya saṃvattati, tasmā vuttaṃ “channaṃ…pe… vihaññatī”ti.

70. "In what?" (kismiṃ) means "when what exists?" (kismiṃ sati). But its existence is solely by way of arising, thus it is said, "When what arises?" (kismiṃ uppanne). The world is said to arise, because the designation 'world' is without clinging. "In the six" (chasu): here too, the same principle applies. "Intimacy" (santhavaṃ) means it causes excessive affection, because the internal sense bases are the object of excessive affection. "Dependent on" (upādāya): this is a gerund that requires a subsequent action; by way of ellipsis, the verb "proceeds" (pavattati) is taken. But what proceeds? The world, meaning the designation of the world. "In the six" (chasu): this is a locative in the sense of cause. For the six sense bases are the cause of all suffering. "This" (ayaṃ) means the world of beings. It is called "arisen" (uppanno) because the six sense bases are the root of all suffering. In the external sense bases it creates intimacy, especially because forms, etc., are objects of craving. Because, by way of gratifying the eye, etc., and because of apprehending forms, etc., it leads to the world being frequented, therefore it is said, "Because of the six... one is afflicted."

Lokasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Loka Sutta is finished.

Addhavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Addha Vagga is finished.

8. Chetvāvaggo

8. The Chetvā Vagga

1. Chetvāsuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Chetvā Sutta

71. Vadhitvāti hantvā vināsetvā. Aparidayhamānattāti apīḷiyamānattā. Vinaṭṭhadomanassattā na socati cetodukkhadukkhābhāvato. Visaṃ nāma dukkhaṃ aniṭṭhabhāvato, tassa mūlakāraṇaṃ kodho aniṭṭhaphalattāti āha “visamūlassāti dukkhavipākassā”ti. Akkuṭṭhassāti akkosāparādhassa. Akkosapahāratthasambandhena hi “kuddhassā”ti upayogatthe sampadānavacanaṃ. Sukhaṃ uppajjati kodhaṃ nassati. Sukhuppattiṃ sandhāya esa kodho “madhuraggo”ti vutto, sukhāvasānoti attho.

71. "Having slain" (vadhitvā) means "having killed, having destroyed." "Because of not being burned" (aparidayhamānattā) means "because of not being oppressed." Because his dejection is destroyed, "he does not grieve" (na socati), due to the absence of the suffering of mental pain. "Poison" (visaṃ) is suffering, because of its undesirable nature; its root cause is anger, because it has an undesirable result. Hence, it is said, "rooted in poison" (visamūlassa), meaning "of that which has a painful result." "Of abuse" (akkuṭṭhassa) means "of the offense of abuse." For in connection with the meaning of abuse and assault, the word "for the angry" (kuddhassa) is a dative case in the sense of purpose. Happiness arises when anger ceases. With reference to the arising of happiness, this anger is called "sweet-tipped" (madhuraggo), meaning it has a pleasant end.

Chetvāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Chetvā Sutta is finished.

2. Rathasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Explanation of the Ratha Sutta

72. Paññāṇanti lakkhaṇaṃ sallakkhaṇūpāyo. Disvāti dassanahetu. “Coḷarañño raṭṭhaṃ coḷaraṭṭha”nti evaṃ raṭṭhaṃ raññā paññāyati.

72. "A sign" (paññāṇaṃ) means "a mark," "a means of discerning." "Having seen" (disvā) means "the cause of seeing." "The kingdom of King Coḷa is the Coḷa kingdom"—thus, the kingdom is known by the king.

Rathasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Ratha Sutta is finished.

3. Vittasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Explanation of the Vitta Sutta

73. Saddhāyāti [M 1.0136] saddhāhetu. Kulasampadāti khattiyādisampattiyo. Sabbalokiyalokuttaravittapaṭilābhahetuto saddhāvittameva. Heṭṭhā tiṇṇaṃ dvārānaṃ vasena uppannakassa sabbassapi anavajjadhammassa saṅgaṇhanato “dhammoti dasakusalakammapatho”ti vuttaṃ. Asaṃkiliṭṭhasukhanti. Nirāmisaṃ [V 1.0120] sukhaṃ. Tameva sāmisaṃ upanidhāya sambhāvento āha “asaṃkiliṭṭha”nti. Asecanakabhāvena abhirucijananato piyākicchakaraṇato bahuṃ sucirampi kālaṃ āsevantassa adosāvahato saccameva madhurataraṃ. Na hi taṃ pivitabbato sāditabbato anubhavitabbato rasoti vattabbataṃ arahati. Idāni tassa kiccasampattiatthehipi mahārahataṃ dassetuṃ “saccasmiṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha nadīnivattanaṃ mahākappinavatthuādīhi (dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.mahākappinattheravatthu; a. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.231; theragā. aṭṭha. 2.mahākappinattheragāthāvaṇṇanā) dīpetabbaṃ, itarāni kaṇhadīpāyanajātaka- (jā. 1.10.62 ādayo) sutasoma- (jā. 2.21.371 ādayo) macchajātakehi (jā. 1.1.34, 75; 1.2.131 ādayo) dīpetabbāni. Nimmaddenti abhibhavanti. Madhurataranti sundarataraṃ seṭṭhesūti attho. Paññājīvīti paññāya jīvanasīloti paññājīvī, paññāpubbaṅgamacariyoti attho. Paññājīvīti ca paññāvasena iriyati vattati jīvitaṃ pavattetīti atthoti dassento “yo paññājīvī”tiādimāha. “Jīvata”nti keci paṭhanti, jīvantānaṃ paññājīviṃ seṭṭhamāhūti attho.

73. "By faith" (saddhāya) means "because of faith." "Accomplishment of family" (kulasampadā) refers to the accomplishments of the khattiyas and others. Because it is the cause for gaining all worldly and supramundane wealth, it is indeed faith-wealth. Because it includes all blameless qualities that have arisen by way of the three doors, it is said, "Dhamma means the tenfold path of wholesome actions." "Uncorrupted happiness" (asaṃkiliṭṭhasukhaṃ) means non-sensual happiness. Considering it in comparison with sensual happiness, he said "uncorrupted." Because it is satisfying in itself, generates delight, does what is pleasing, and brings no fault to one who cultivates it for a very long time, truth is indeed sweeter. For it does not deserve to be called a 'taste' on account of being something to be drunk, savored, or experienced. Now, to show its great value also in terms of accomplishing its function, "For in truth," etc., was said. Here, "the turning back of rivers" (nadīnivattanaṃ) should be illustrated by stories like that of Mahākappina (DhA. 1; AN. 1.231; ThagA. 2), while the others should be illustrated by the Kaṇhadīpāyana Jātaka (Jā. 1.10.62), Sutasoma Jātaka (Jā. 2.21.371), and Maccha Jātaka (Jā. 1.1.34, 75; 1.2.131). "They overwhelm" (nimmaddenti) means "they overcome." "Sweeter" (madhurataraṃ) means "more beautiful, the best among them." "One who lives by wisdom" (paññājīvī) means one whose habit is to live by wisdom; the meaning is his conduct is preceded by wisdom. And showing that "one who lives by wisdom" means one who acts, behaves, and carries on his life by means of wisdom, he said, "who lives by wisdom," etc. Some read "jīvataṃ," meaning: "among the living, they say the one who lives by wisdom is best."

Vittasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Vitta Sutta is finished.

4. Vuṭṭhisuttavaṇṇanā

4. Explanation of the Vuṭṭhi Sutta

74. Uppatantānanti pathaviṃ bhinditvā uṭṭhahantānaṃ. “Seṭṭha”nti vuccamānattā “sattavidha”nti vuttaṃ, itaresaṃ vā tadanulomato. Khemo hoti dubbhikkhupaddavābhāvato. Tenāha “subhikkho”ti. Nipatantānanti adhomukhaṃ pavattantānaṃ. Pavajamānānanti vajanasīlānaṃ. Te pana yasmā jaṅgamā nāma honti, na rukkhādayo viya thāvarā, tasmā āha “jaṅgamāna”nti. Gāvoti dhenuyo. Tena mahiṃsādikānampi saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo. Vadantānanti uppannaṃ atthaṃ vadantānaṃ.

74. "Of those flying up" (uppatantānaṃ) means of those rising up, breaking through the earth. Because it is called "supreme," it is said to be "sevenfold," or for others in accordance with that. "It is secure" (khemo hoti) because of the absence of the calamity of famine; thus it is said "abundant" (subhikkho). "Of those falling down" (nipatantānaṃ) means of those proceeding downwards. "Of those who go forth" (pavajamānānaṃ) means of those who are accustomed to go. But since they are called "moving beings" (jaṅgamā), not stationary like trees and so forth, thus it is said "of moving beings" (jaṅgamānaṃ). "Cattle" (gāvo) means cows; by that, the inclusion of buffaloes and the like should be understood. "Of those who speak" (vadantānaṃ) means of those who speak on a matter that has arisen.

Attano [M 1.0137] khantiyāti attano khantiyā ruciyā gahitabhāvena. Itarā devatā tassā vissajjane aparitussamānā āha. Yāva padhaṃsīti guṇadhaṃsī satthudesanāya laddhabbaguṇanāsanato. Pagabbāti pāgabbiyena samannāgatā, yathā vacīpāgabbiyena akharā, tathā vācāya bhavitabbaṃ. Mukharāti mukhakharā. Dasabalaṃ pucchi saṇhaṃ sukhumaṃ ratanattayasaṃhitaṃ atthaṃ sotukāmā. Assā devatāya vissajjento ajjhāsayānurūpaṃ. Uppatamānāti uppatantī samugghāṭeti odhiso. Vaṭṭamūlakamahāavijjāti tassā ādīnavadassanatthaṃ bhūtakathanavisesanaṃ. Osīdantānanti paṭipakkhavasena adho sīdantānaṃ, ussādayamānānanti attho. Puññakkhettabhūtoti idaṃ “padasā caramānāna”nti [V 1.0121] padassa atthavivaraṇavasena bhūtakathanavisesanaṃ. Yādiso putto vā hotūti idaṃ purimapade devatāya puttagahaṇassa katattā vuttaṃ.

"Attano khantiyā" means by one's own patience, inclination, and acceptance. The other deity, being dissatisfied with her explanation, said: "Yāva padhaṃsī" means a destroyer of virtues, because of the destruction of good qualities that should be obtained from the Teacher's teaching. "Pagabbā" means possessing presumption; speech should be like that, with verbal presumption and harshness. "Mukharā" means harsh-mouthed. Desiring to hear the gentle, subtle meaning connected with the Triple Gem, she asked the Ten-Powered One. Explaining in accordance with that deity's inclination: "Uppatamānā" means rising up, she uncovers specifically. "The great ignorance whose root is the round of existence" is a specific statement of reality for the purpose of showing its danger. "Osīdantānaṃ" means of those sinking downwards due to opposing forces; the meaning is "of those who are uplifting." "Being a field of merit" is a specific statement of reality by way of explaining the meaning of the phrase "walking on foot." "May such a son be" is said because the deity had made mention of taking a son in the preceding phrase.

Vuṭṭhisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Vuṭṭhi Sutta is concluded.

5. Bhītāsuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Bhītā Sutta

75. Kiṃ sūdha bhītāti ettha su-idhāti nipātamattanti āha “kiṃ bhītā”ti? Maggo ca nekāyatanappavuttoti anekakāraṇaṃ nānāvidhādhigamokāsaṃ katvā pavutto kathito. Tenāha “aṭṭhatiṃsārammaṇavasenā”tiādi. Evaṃ santeti evaṃ sabbasādhāraṇānekāyatanehi nibbānagāmimaggassa tumhehi paveditattā labbhamāne kheme magge kiṃ bhītāyaṃ janatā uppathabhūtā viparītadiṭṭhito gaṇhīti attho? Evaṃ devatā yathicchāya purimaddhena attanā yathācintitamatthaṃ satthu paveditā, pacchimaddhena attano saṃsayaṃ pucchati. Bahupaññāti puthupañña. Ussannapaññāti adhikapaññā. Ṭhapetvāti saṃyametvā. Saṃvibhāgīti āhāraparibhoge sammadeva vibhajanasīlo. Tenāha “accharāyā”tiādi. Vuttatthameva heṭṭhā.

75. "Kiṃ sūdha bhītā"—here, "su-idhā" is merely a particle, thus it is said, "Why afraid?" "The path is also proclaimed as proceeding through various means" means that having made various causes and diverse opportunities for attainment, it is proclaimed, it is taught. Thus he says, "by means of thirty-eight objects," and so forth. "Evaṃ sante" means: "This being so, since the path leading to Nibbāna has been proclaimed by you through various common means, why is this populace, having gone astray and being seized by wrong views, afraid when a safe path is attainable?" This is the meaning. Thus, the deity, as she wished, conveyed the meaning she had in mind to the Teacher through the first half of the verse, and in the latter half, she asks her own doubt. "Bahupaññā" means of broad wisdom. "Ussannapaññā" means of superior wisdom. "Ṭhapetvā" means having restrained. "Saṃvibhāgī" means by nature one who properly distributes in the use of food. Thus he says, "with a snap of the fingers," and so forth. The meaning is as stated below.

Manenāti manogahaṇena. Pubbasuddhiaṅganti pubbabhāgasuddhibhūtaṃ aṅgaṃ. Catūsūti vuttaaṅgapariyāpannaṃ. Yaññaupakkharoti dānassa sādhanaṃ. Etesu dhammesūti [M 1.0138] etesu saddhādiguṇesu. Yathā hi saddho paccayaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā vatthupariccāgassa visesapaccayo kammaphalassa paralokassa ca paccakkhato viya pattiyāyanato, evaṃ muduhadayo. Muduhadayo hi anudayaṃ patvā yaṃ kiñci attano santakaṃ paresaṃ deti. Yo ca saṃvibhāgasīlo, so appakasmimpi attano santake parehi sādhāraṇabhogī hoti. Vadaññū vadāniyatāya yāginova yuttaṃ yuttakālaṃ ñatvā atthikānaṃ manorathaṃ pūretīti vuttaṃ “iti…pe… catūsūti āhā”ti.

"Manena" means by mental grasping. "Pubbasuddhiaṅgaṃ" means the factor that is the preliminary purification. "Catūsu" means included within the stated factors. "Yaññaupakkharo" means the means for giving. "Etesu dhammesu" refers to these qualities such as faith and so forth. For just as a faithful person, having established a condition, is a special condition for the relinquishing of possessions because he trusts in the fruit of action and the next world as if seeing them directly, so too is a tender-hearted person. A tender-hearted person, having attained compassion, gives to others whatever he possesses. And one who is by nature inclined to sharing makes even the smallest of his possessions common for others. "Vadaññū" means that, due to his liberality, knowing what is fitting and the appropriate time, he fulfills the wishes of those in need. Thus it is said, "as... up to... in the four," he says.

Vācantiādīni tīṇi aṅgāni tividhasīlasampattidīpanato. Sampannasīlo hi paralokaṃ na bhāseyya. Saddho ekaṃ aṅgaṃ payogāsayasuddhidīpanato. Suddhāsayassa sammāpayoge ṭhitassa kathaṃ paralokato bhayanti. Dukavasena caturaṅgayojanā dukanayo. Etesu catūsu dhammesu ṭhitoti etesu yathāvuttadukasaṅgahesu catūsu guṇesu patiṭṭhito.

The three factors beginning with speech explain the threefold perfection of virtue. For one whose virtue is perfected would not fear the next world. Faith is one factor, explaining the purification of effort and intention. How could there be fear of the next world for one established in right effort with pure intention? The application of the four factors by way of the dyad is the method of the dyad. "Established in these four qualities" means established in these four virtues as explained in the twofold summary.

Bhītāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bhītā Sutta is concluded.

6. Najīratisuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Najīrati Sutta

76. Nāmagottanti [V 1.0122] tisso kassapo gotamoti evarūpaṃ nāmañca gottañca. Nidassanamattametaṃ, tasmā sabbassa paññattiyā lakkhaṇavacananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Na jīratīti asabhāvadhammattā uppādavayābhāvato jaraṃ na pāpuṇāti. Tenāha “jīraṇasabhāvo na hotī”ti. Yasmā samaññābhāvato kālantarepi taṃ samaññāyateva, tasmā “atītabuddhānaṃ…pe… na jīratīti vuccatī”ti āha.

76. "Nāmagottaṃ" means Tissa, Kassapa, Gotama, and such names and clans. This is merely an illustration; therefore, it should be regarded as a term defining the characteristic of all designations. "It does not decay" means that, because it is not a real phenomenon and is without arising and passing away, it does not reach decay. Thus he says, "It does not have the nature of decay." Since, due to the existence of the designation, it is designated in the same way even after a long time, he therefore says, "Concerning the Buddhas of the past...it is said not to decay."

Ālasiyanti alasabhāvo daḷhakosajjaṃ. Tenāha “yenā”tiādi. Ṭhitinti byāpāraṃ. Niddāvasena pamajjanaṃ kattabbassa akaraṇaṃ. Kilesavasena pamajjanaṃ akattabbassa karaṇampi. Kammasamayeti kammaṃ kātuṃ yuttakāle. Kammakaraṇavīriyābhāvoti taṃkammakiriyasamuṭṭhāpakavīriyābhāvo. So pana atthato vīriyapaṭipakkho akusalacittuppādo, na vīriyassa abhāvamattaṃ. Sīlasaññamābhāvo dussīlyaṃ. Vissaṭṭhācāratā nāma anācāro. Soppabahulatāti niddālutā[M 1.0139]. Yato gahaṇahatthopi na kilāsupi puriso niddāya abhibhuyyati. Tenāha “tāyā”tiādi. Aticchātādīnīti ādi-saddena abhibhuyyatādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Āgantukālasiyaṃ na pubbe vuttaālasyaṃ viya pakatisiddhaṃ. “Te chidde”ti pāḷiyaṃ liṅgavipallāsena vuttanti āha “tāni cha chiddānī”ti. Kusalacittappavattiyā anokāsabhāvato chiddāni. Tenāha bhagavā – “yattha vittaṃ na tiṭṭhatī”ti. Sabbākārena lesamattaṃ asesetvāti adhippāyo.

"Ālasiyaṃ" means the state of being lazy, a strong indolence. Thus he says, "by which," and so forth. "Ṭhiti" means occupation. Negligence due to sleep is the non-performance of what should be done. Negligence due to defilements is also the performance of what should not be done. "Kammasamaye" means at the suitable time to do the work. "The absence of energy for doing work" means the lack of energy that initiates the performance of that work. However, in essence, it is the arising of unwholesome consciousness opposed to energy, not merely the absence of energy. The absence of virtue and restraint is immorality. "Vissaṭṭhācāratā" is called improper conduct. "Soppabahulatā" means being prone to sleep. Because even a man with something in his hand, though not tired, is overcome by sleep. Thus he says, "by that," and so forth. "Aticchātādīni" includes "being overwhelmed and so forth" by the word "ādi." Transient laziness is not inherent like the previously mentioned laziness. "'Te chidde' in the Pāli text is stated with a reversal of gender; thus he says, 'tāni cha chiddāni' (those six holes)." They are holes because they provide no opportunity for the arising of wholesome consciousness. Thus the Blessed One said, "where wealth does not remain." The intention is: leaving no remainder at all, not even a trace.

Najīratisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Najīrati Sutta is concluded.

7. Issariyasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Issariya Sutta

77. Satthassa malanti satthamalaṃ, yena satthaṃ malīnaṃ hoti, satthamalaggahaṇena cettha malīnaṃ satthameva gahitanti āha “malaggahitasattha”nti. Āṇāpavattananti appake vā mahante vā yattha katthaci attano āṇāya pavattanavasena vasanaṃ issariyattamicchanti. Maṇiratanampi vissajjanīyapakkhikattā uttamaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ nāma na hoti, itthī pana pariccattakulācāritthikāyapi anissajjanīyatāya uttamabhaṇḍaṃ nāma. Tenāha “itthī bhaṇḍānamuttama”nti. Tesaṃ tesañhi purisājānīyānaṃ uppattiṭṭhānatāya uttamaratanākarattā itthī bhaṇḍānamuttamaṃ. Malaggahitasatthasadiso avabodhakiccavibandhanato. Satthamalaṃ viya satthassa paññāsatthassa guṇābhāvakaraṇato paññāsatthamalaṃ[V 1.0123]. Abbu vuccati upaddavaṃ, taṃ detīti abbudaṃ, vināsakāraṇaṃ. Nanu haraṇaṃ samaṇassa ayuttanti? Yuttaṃ. Tassa anvayato byatirekato ca yuttataṃ dassento “salākabhattādīnī”tiādimāha.

77. The rust of a knife is called 'knife-rust'; by it a knife becomes rusty. By the mention of 'knife-rust' here, a rusty knife itself is meant. Hence it is said, 'a knife seized by rust.' The wielding of authority means desiring sovereignty by dwelling in such a way that one's own command prevails anywhere, whether in small or large matters. Even a jewel treasure is not called the highest possession because it belongs to the class of things that can be relinquished. But a woman, even one who has abandoned the conduct of her family, is called the highest possession because she cannot be relinquished. Hence it is said, 'A woman is the highest of possessions.' For because she is the place of origin of those noble men, and because she is a mine of supreme gems, a woman is the highest of possessions. It obstructs the function of understanding, like a knife seized by rust. Just as knife-rust causes the knife—the wisdom-knife—to be without qualities, so is the rust of wisdom. 'Abbu' is called a calamity; it gives that, hence it is 'abbudaṃ,' a cause of destruction. Surely, is taking things unfitting for a renunciant? It is fitting. To show its fittingness by way of agreement and disagreement, he said, 'alms-food tickets and so forth.'

Issariyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Issariya Sutta is concluded.

8. Kāmasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Kāma Sutta

78. “Attakāmo”ti [M 1.0140] pāḷiyaṃ vuttattā āha “ṭhapetvā sabbabodhisatte”ti. Te hi sabbaso paratthāya eva paṭipajjamānā mahākāruṇikā paratthakāmā, atthakāmā nāma na honti, yā ca tesaṃ attatthāvahā paṭipatti, sāpi yāvadeva paratthā evāti. Vuttaṃ porāṇaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Yasmā bodhisattā parahitapaṭipattiyā pāramiyo pūrentā tathārūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ patvā attānaṃ paresaṃ pariccajanti paññāpāramiyā paripūraṇato, tasmā idhāpi “sabbabodhisatte ṭhapetvāyevāti vutta”nti āha. Kalyāṇanti bhaddakaṃ. Vācāya adhippetattā āha “saṇhaṃ muduka”nti. Pāpikanti lāmakaṃ nihīnaṃ. Taṃ pana pharusaṃ vācanti sarūpato dasseti.

78. Because the word 'attakāmo' is stated in the Pāḷi, it is said, 'excluding all Bodhisattas.' For they, practicing entirely for the sake of others, are greatly compassionate and desire the good of others; they are not called self-interested. And whatever practice of theirs brings about their own good, that too is solely for the sake of others. This is stated in the ancient commentary. Because Bodhisattas, fulfilling the perfections through practices for the welfare of others, upon reaching such a cause, sacrifice themselves for others due to the fulfillment of the perfection of wisdom, therefore here too he says, 'it is said, 'excluding all Bodhisattas'.' 'Kalyāṇa' means good. Because speech is intended, it is said to be 'gentle and soft.' 'Pāpika' means base and inferior. That, however, is shown in its nature as 'harsh speech'.

Kāmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Kāma Sutta is concluded.

9. Pātheyyasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Explanation of the Pātheyya Sutta

79. Saddhā bandhati pātheyyanti saddhā nāma sattassa maraṇavasena mahāpathaṃ saṃvajato mahākantāraṃ paṭipajjato mahāviduggaṃ pakkhandato pātheyyapuṭaṃ bandhati sambalaṃ sajjeti. Kathanti āha “saddhaṃ uppādetvā”tiādi. Etaṃ vuttanti “saddhā bandhati pātheyya”nti etaṃ gāthāpadaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā. Sirīti katapuññehi sevīyati tehi paṭilabhīyatīti sirī. Issariyaṃ vibhavo. Āsayitabbato āsayo, vasanaṭṭhānaṃ niketanti attho. Parikaḍḍhatīti icchāvasikaṃ puggalaṃ tattha tattha upakaḍḍhati.

79. The phrase 'faith binds provisions' means that faith, indeed, binds a bundle of provisions and prepares supplies for a being who is journeying on the great path by way of death, entering the great wilderness, and plunging into the great difficult passage. How? He said, 'Having aroused faith,' and so forth. This was stated: this verse-line, 'faith binds provisions,' was spoken by the Blessed One. 'Sirī' is so called because it is served by those who have done merit, and it is attained by them. Sovereignty is prosperity. 'Āsaya' is so called because it is to be resorted to; the meaning is a dwelling place, a home. 'Parikaḍḍhati' means it draws a person subject to desire here and there.

Pātheyyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Pātheyya Sutta is concluded.

10. Pajjotasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Explanation of the Pajjota Sutta

80. Taṃ taṃ samavisamaṃ pajjotatīti pajjoto. Padīpo andhakāraṃ vidhamitvā paccakkhato rūpagataṃ dasseti, evaṃ paññāpajjoto avijjandhakāraṃ vidhamitvā dhammānaṃ paramatthabhūtaṃ [V 1.0124] rūpaṃ dasseti. Jāgarabrāhmaṇo viyāti jāgarakhīṇāsavabrāhmaṇo viya. So hi satipaññāvepullappattiyā sabbadāpi jāgaro hoti. Gāvoti gojātiyo. Idaṃ [M 1.0141] gunnaṃ goṇānañca sāmaññato gahaṇaṃ. Kammeti karaṇatthe bhummavacanaṃ. Jīvanaṃ jīvo, saha jīvenāti sajīvino. Tenāha “kammena saha jīvantāna”nti, kasivāṇijjādikammaṃ katvā jīvantānanti attho. Gomaṇḍalehi saddhinti gogaṇena saha. Na tena vinā kasikammādīni uppajjanti, gorasasiddhiyā ceva kasanabhāravahanasiddhiyā ca kasikammaekaccavāṇijjakammādīni ijjhanti. Sattakāyassāti āhārupajīvino sattakāyassa kasito aññathā jīvikaṃ kappentassapi kasijīvitavuttiyā mūlakāraṇaṃ phalanipphattinimittattā tassa. Iriyāpatho ca iriyanakiriyānaṃ pavattanupāyo. “Sītanti naṅgalasītakamma”nti vadanti.

80. Because it illuminates various things, the even and the uneven, it is called 'pajjota' (light). Just as a lamp dispels darkness and directly reveals visible forms, so too the light of wisdom dispels the darkness of ignorance and reveals the ultimate nature of phenomena. 'Like an awakened brahmin' means like an awakened brahmin whose taints are destroyed. For he is always alert, having attained the fullness of mindfulness and wisdom. 'Gāvo' refers to the bovine species. This is a general term for both cows and oxen. 'Kamma' is a locative case in the sense of 'doing.' 'Jīvanaṃ' means life; 'sajīvino' means 'with life.' Hence it is said, 'of those who live by work,' meaning those who live by engaging in farming, trade, and so forth. 'With herds of cattle' means along with a herd of cattle. Without them, farming and other tasks do not arise, for by the success of milk products and the success of plowing and carrying loads, farming and certain trade activities succeed. 'Of the group of beings' means that for the group of beings that subsists on food, even for one who makes a livelihood in a way other than farming, farming is the root cause of livelihood because it is the cause for the production of results for that livelihood. And 'iriyāpatha' (manner of movement) is the means by which the actions of moving are carried out. They say, ''Sīta' means the work of plowing with a plow'.

Pajjotasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Pajjota Sutta is concluded.

11. Araṇasuttavaṇṇanā

11. Explanation of the Araṇa Sutta

81. Raṇanti kandanti etehīti raṇā, rāgādayo. Tehi abhibhūtatāya hi sattā nānappakāraṃ kandanti paridevanti. Te pana sabbaso natthi etesaṃ raṇāti araṇā. Nikkilesā khīṇāsavā. Vusitavāsoti vusitabrahmacariyavāso. Bhojissiyanti bhujissabhāvo. Tenāha “adāsabhāvo”ti. Samaṇāti samitapāpasamaṇāti āha “khīṇāsavasamaṇā”ti. Puthujjanakalyāṇakāle lokiyapariññāya, sekkhā pubbabhāge lokiyapariññāya, paccavekkhaṇe lokiyalokuttarāya pariññāya pariññeyyaṃ tebhūmakaṃ khandhapañcakaṃ parijānanti paricchijjanti. Khīṇāsavā pana pariññātapariññeyyā honti. Tathā hi te sāmī hutvā paribhuñjanti. Vandanti naṃ patiṭṭhitanti vuttaṃ, vandanīyabhāvo ca sīlasampannatāyāti āha “patiṭṭhitanti sīle patiṭṭhita”nti. Idhāti imasmiṃ loke. Khattiyāti lakkhaṇavacananti āha “na kevalaṃ khattiyāvā”tiādi.

81. Because of these they cry, hence 'raṇā' (cries)—referring to lust and other defilements. Indeed, beings, overwhelmed by these, cry and lament in various ways. But for them, these cries are entirely absent—thus, they are 'araṇā' (free from cries). They are without defilements, those whose taints are destroyed. 'Vusitavāso' means the living of the holy life has been lived. 'Bhojissiya' means the state of freedom. Therefore, it is said, 'the state of not being a slave.' 'Samaṇā' refers to ascetics who have pacified evil—hence, it is said, 'ascetics whose taints are destroyed.' At the time of being virtuous worldlings, by means of worldly full understanding; trainees, in the preliminary stage, by means of worldly full understanding; and during reviewing, by means of worldly and supramundane full understanding, they fully know and delineate the five aggregates belonging to the three planes, which are to be fully understood. But those whose taints are destroyed have fully understood what is to be understood. Indeed, they, as masters, make use of it. 'They revere him, established'—this is said; and the state of being worthy of veneration is due to being endowed with virtue—hence, it is said, ''established' means established in virtue.' 'Idha' means in this world. 'Khattiya' is a term denoting a characteristic—hence, it is said, 'not only khattiyas,' and so forth.

Araṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Araṇa Sutta is concluded.

Chetvāvaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Chetvāvagga is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

Of the Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya

Devatāsaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Elucidation of the Hidden Meanings in the Commentary on the Devatā Saṃyutta is concluded.

2. Devaputtasaṃyuttaṃ

2. The Devaputta Saṃyutta

1. Paṭhamavaggo

1. The First Chapter

1. Paṭhamakassapasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the First Kassapa Sutta

82. Devassa [V 1.0125][M 1.0142] putto devaputto. Devānaṃ janakajanetabbasambandhābhāvato kathamayaṃ devaputtoti vuccatīti āha “devānaṃ hī”tiādi. “Apākaṭo aññataroti vuccatī”ti idaṃ yebhuyyavasena vuttaṃ. Pākaṭopi hi katthaci “aññataro”ti vuccati. Heṭṭhā devatāsaṃyutte “apākaṭā aññatarā devatā”ti vatvā idha “pākaṭo devaputto”ti vuttaṃ. Tathā hissa kassapoti gottanāmaṃ gahitaṃ, tañca kho purimajātisiddhasamaññāvasena. Anusāsanaṃ anusāso, taṃ anusāsaṃ. Bhikkhuniddesanti bhikkhusaddassa niddesaṃ. Bhikkhuovādanti bhikkhubhāvāvahaṃ ovādaṃ. Yadi pana na assosi, kathamayaṃ pañhaṃ kathesīti? Aññato sutaṃ nissāya pañhaṃ kathesi, na pana bhagavato sammukhā sutabhāvena.

82. A son of a deva is a devaputta. Due to the absence of a parent-child relationship among the devas, how is this one called a devaputta? It is said, 'For the devas indeed,' and so forth. 'An unmanifest one is called 'a certain one''—this is said for the most part. For even a manifest one is sometimes called 'a certain one.' Previously, in the Devatāsaṃyutta, it was said, 'an unmanifest certain devatā,' but here it is said, 'a manifest devaputta.' Thus his clan name Kassapa is taken; and that is by way of a designation established in a previous birth. 'Anusāsanaṃ' means 'anusāso,' that is, instruction. 'Bhikkhuniddesaṃ' is the explanation of the word 'bhikkhu.' 'Bhikkhuovādaṃ' is advice that brings about the state of a bhikkhu. But if he did not hear, how did he state this question? He stated the question based on what he had heard from another, not from having heard it in the presence of the Blessed One.

Tesanti yathāvuttānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ. “Kathetukāmo cevā”tiādinā hi catutthaṃ idha uddhaṭaṃ. Tattha ādito tiṇṇaṃ bhagavā pañhaṃ bhāraṃ na karoti ekekaṅgavekallato ceva aṅgadvayavekallato ca, catutthassa pana ubhayaṅgapāripūrattā bhāraṃ karotīti āha “ayaṃ panā”tiādi.

'Tesaṃ' refers to the three types of individuals as described. For by the phrase 'and wishing to speak,' and so forth, the fourth is cited here. In this context, the Blessed One does not make the question a burden for the first three, because of a deficiency in one factor and a deficiency in two factors. But for the fourth, because of the completeness of both factors, He makes it a burden—thus it is said, 'But this one,' and so forth.

Gāthāyaṃ “subhāsitassā”ti upayogatthe sāmivacananti āha “subhāsitaṃ sikkheyyā”ti. Catusaccādinissitaṃ buddhavacanaṃ sikkhanto catubbidhaṃ vacīsucaritaṃ sikkhati nāmāti āha “catusaccanissitaṃ…pe… sikkheyyā”ti. Avadhāraṇena tappaṭipakkhaṃ paṭinivatteti. Upāsitabbanti āsevitabbaṃ bhāvetabbaṃ bahulīkātabbaṃ. Aṭṭhatiṃsabhedaṃ kammaṭṭhānanti idaṃ tassa vipassanāpadaṭṭhānataṃ hadaye ṭhapetvā vuttaṃ. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “dutiyapadena adhipaññāsikkhā kathitā”ti. Ye pana “dutiyapadena adhicittasikkhā cittavūpasamena adhipaññāsikkhā”ti [V 1.0126] paṭhanti, tesaṃ padena aṭṭhatiṃsappabhedakammaṭṭhānaṃ suddhasamathakammaṭṭhānasseva gahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yadi evaṃ “aṭṭhasamāpattivasenā”ti idaṃ kathanti? “Taṃ vipassanādhiṭṭhānānaṃ samāpattīnaṃ vasena [M 1.0143] kathita”nti vadanti. Evañca katvā “dutiyapadena adhipaññāsikkhā”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ samatthitaṃ hoti. Sikkhanaṃ nāma āsevananti āha “bhāveyyāti attho”ti. Upāsananti payirupāsanaṃ. Tañca kho assutapariyāpuṇanakammaṭṭhānuggahādivasena dassento “tampī”tiādimāha. Adhisīlasikkhā kathitā lakkhaṇahāranayena. Vacīsucaritassa hi sīlasabhāvattā taggahaṇeneva tadekalakkhaṇaṃ kāyasucaritampi itarampi gahitamevāti. Ettha ca adhisīlasikkhāya cittaviveko, adhipaññāsikkhāya upadhiviveko, adhicittasikkhāya kāyaviveko kathito, kāyaviveko pana sarūpeneva pāḷiyaṃ gahitoti tividhassapi vivekassa pakāsitattaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

In the verse, the genitive case in 'subhāsitassa' is used in the sense of the object; hence it is said, 'one should train in what is well-spoken.' By training in the Buddha's words, which are grounded in the Four Truths and so forth, one trains in the fourfold good conduct of speech—thus it is said, 'grounded in the Four Truths... one should train.' By way of emphasis, one turns away from its opposite. 'Upāsitabba' means it should be frequented, developed, and made much of. The thirty-eight types of meditation subjects are mentioned here, having placed their basis for insight in the heart. For it is said, 'by the second line, the training in higher wisdom is taught.' But for those who read, 'by the second line, the training in higher mind is taught; through the calming of the mind, the training in higher wisdom,' it should be understood that the line refers only to the pure serenity meditation subjects, comprised of the thirty-eight types. If so, how is the phrase 'by means of the eight attainments' explained? They say, 'It is spoken of in relation to the attainments that serve as the basis for insight.' Thus, the statement 'by the second line, the training in higher wisdom is taught' is justified. 'Training' means repeated practice—hence it is said, 'the meaning is "one should develop."' 'Upāsana' means attending upon. Illustrating this through learning, mastering, and undertaking meditation subjects, it is said, 'that too.' The training in higher virtue has been explained by the method of characteristic. Since good conduct of speech is essentially virtuous, by grasping that, bodily good conduct and the other, which have the same characteristic, are also grasped. Here, through the training in higher virtue, mental seclusion is taught; through the training in higher wisdom, seclusion from the substrates of existence; and through the training in higher mind, bodily seclusion is taught. Bodily seclusion, however, is directly stated in the Pāli itself. Thus, the threefold seclusion is made clear. The rest is easily understood.

Paṭhamakassapasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the First Kassapa Sutta is concluded.

2. Dutiyakassapasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Second Kassapa Sutta

83. Dvīhi jhānehīti ārammaṇalakkhaṇūpanijjhānalakkhaṇehi dvīhi jhānehi. Kammaṭṭhānavimuttiyāti kammaṭṭhānānuyogaladdhāya vimuttiyā. Tena tadaṅgavikkhambhanavimuttiyo vadati. Satthusāsanassa hadayattā abbhantarattā hadayassa mānasassa, anupattiṃ paṭilābhamānasaṃ. Taṃ pana atthato aññā evāti āha “arahatta”nti. Taṃ pattukāmena ekantato vajjetabbataṇhādiṭṭhīnaṃ bhāve tassa anijjhanato, tadabhāve ijjhanato ca te uppādanavasena yadaggena nissito, tadaggena panāyampi tehi nissito nāma hotīti āha “anissito”tiādi. Arahattaṃ ānisaṃsitabbaṭṭhena ānisaṃsaṃ etassāti arahattānisaṃso. Arahattaṃ pattukāmassa pubbabhāgapaṭipadā icchitabbā. Tattha ca sabbapaṭhamo kammaṭṭhānaattānuyogo, so idha na gahitoti āha “tantidhammo pubbabhāgo”ti. Tattha tantidhammoti pariyattidhammo.

83. By two kinds of jhāna: by the two jhānas characterized by the object and by close contemplation. Liberation through the meditation subject: liberation attained through application to the meditation subject. By this, he speaks of liberation by substitution and liberation by suppression. Because it is the heart of the Teacher’s dispensation, the inner core, it is the mind that desires the attainment, the acquisition, of that heart. But that, in meaning, is final knowledge; therefore he says 'arahantship.' Since, for one who wishes to attain it, its non-attainment is due to the presence of craving and views which must be completely abandoned, and its attainment is due to their absence, in that he is supported by the supreme goal through their non-arising, he is thereby said to be unsupported by them. Thus he says 'unsupported,' etc. One for whom arahantship is the benefit because it is to be aspired to is 'one who has the benefit of arahantship.' For one desiring to attain arahantship, the preliminary practice is to be wished for. And there, the very first is self-application to the meditation subject, but that is not included here; therefore he says 'the preliminary part is the textual Dhamma.' Here, 'textual Dhamma' means the Dhamma of the scriptures.

Dutiyakassapasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Kassapa Sutta is concluded.

3. Maghasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Magha Sutta

84. Maghoti [M 1.0144] sakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ purimajātianugataṃ. Svevāti sakko eva. Vatenāti mātāpituupaṭṭhānādicārittadhammena[V 1.0127]. Aññeti upadhivepakkapāpadhamme abhibhavitvā. Asuranti indasattubhūtaṃ asuraṃ.

84. 'Magha': this is Sakka's name, following from a previous birth. 'He himself': Sakka himself. 'By Vata': by the practice of virtuous conduct, such as attending to parents. 'Others': having overcome evil things that ripen as substrates of existence. 'The Asura': the Asura, who has become Indra's enemy.

Maghasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Magha Sutta is concluded.

4. Māgadhasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Māgadha Sutta

85. Catutthasuttaṃ vuttatthamevāti devatāsaṃyutte saṃvaṇṇitatthameva, tasmā idha na vattabbo atthoti adhippāyo.

85. The fourth sutta is of the same meaning as what was stated before, that is, the meaning explained in the Devatāsaṃyutta. Therefore, the meaning should not be stated here—this is the intention.

Māgadhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā

The Commentary on the Māgadha Sutta is concluded.

5. Dāmalisuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Dāmali Sutta

86. Tena kāraṇenāti tena padhānena kāraṇabhūtena, padhānakaraṇanimittanti attho. Yaṃ kiñci khuddakampi mahantampi hīnampi paṇītampi bhavaṃ. Āyatapaggahoti dīgharattassa vīriyārambho. Kiccavosānanti kiccaniṭṭhānaṃ. Tathevāti yathā arahattuppattito pubbe, tato pacchāpi tatheva “buddhipaggaho”ti vīriyaṃ daḷhaṃ karotūti kuppadhammaṃ viya maññamāno vadati. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārādiatthaṃ pana vīriyakaraṇaṃ icchitabbameva.

86. 'For that reason': by that principal cause, the principal reason and ground—this is the meaning. Whatever existence, whether small or great, inferior or excellent. 'Persistent exertion': the arousal of energy for a long time. 'Completion of the task': the finishing of the task. 'Just so': just as before the attainment of arahantship, so too afterward, 'with increased resolution,' let him make his energy firm, he says, thinking it to be as if of an unstable nature. However, the exertion of energy for the sake of a pleasant abiding in this very life and so forth is indeed to be wished for.

Asaṃkiṇṇāti avomissā evaṃ aññattha anāgatattā. Tenāha “bhagavatā hī”tiādi. Yadi evaṃ idheva kasmā etaṃ vuttanti āha “idha panā”tiādi. Patiṭṭhanti nadī nāma anavaṭṭhitatīrā, tattha patiṭṭhātabbaṭṭhānaṃ.

'Unmixed': unmingled, because it has not occurred elsewhere in this way. Therefore, he said, 'by the Blessed One,' etc. If so, why was this stated here? He said, 'but here,' etc. 'They stand': a river, by nature, has unstable banks; there is a place within it to stand firm.

Dāmalisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dāmali Sutta is concluded.

6. Kāmadasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Kāmada Sutta

87. Pubbayogāvacaroti [M 1.0145] pubbe yogāvacaro purimattabhāve bhāvanamanuyutto. Ayaṃ kira kassapassa bhagavato sāsane pabbajitvāva bahūni vassasahassāni samaṇadhammaṃ akāsi, na pana visesaṃ nibbattesi. Tamatthaṃ kāraṇena saddhiṃ dassetuṃ “bahalakilesatāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ekantaparisuddhassāti yathā visesāvaho hoti[V 1.0128], evaṃ ekantena parisuddhassa sabbaso anupakkiliṭṭhassa. Sīlena samāhitāti yathā sīlaṃ uparūpari visesāvahaṃ nibbedhabhāgiyañca hoti, evaṃ sammadeva āhitacittā suṭṭhu sampannacittā. Tathābhūtā tena samannāgatā hontīti āha “samupetā”ti. Patiṭṭhitasabhāvāti sekkhattā eva yathādhigatadhammena niccalabhāvena adhiṭṭhitasabhāvā. Mayā tuṭṭhiyā gahitāya devaputto “dullabhā tuṭṭhī”ti vakkhatīti bhagavā “tuṭṭhi hoti sukhāvahā”ti avocāti āha “upari pañhasamuṭṭhāpanattha”nti. Pabbajito rukkhamūliko abbhokāsiko vā anagāriyupeto nāma hoti, senāsane pana vasanto kathanti āha “sattabhūmike”tiādi. Catupaccayasantosoti bhāvanābhiyogasiddho catūsu paccayesu santoso. Tena cittavūpasamena tuṭṭhi laddhāti dasseti. Cittavūpasamabhāvanāyāti cittakilesānaṃ vūpasamakarabhāvanāya, manacchaṭṭhānaṃ indriyānaṃ nibbisevanabhāvakaraṇena savisesaṃ cittassa vūpasamakarabhāvanāya rato manoti yojanā.

87. 'Formerly a meditator' means: in a previous existence, a meditator, one devoted to development.
