In reference to the statement ‘May the venerable Great Brahmā partake,’ he says, ‘What are you muttering?’ and so on. ‘Tiṇabījāni’ refers to rice grains and so forth. ‘Goyūsa’ is said by one who is disgusted with milk. This meaning is also shown by the one who says, ‘This is not the kind of food for a Brahmā.’

Atidevapattopi pañcakhandhūpadhīnaṃ atthitāya kilesūpadhiādīnaṃyeva virahitabhāvo gahito. Aññatra hi bhāvapaccayaṃ tadattho viññāyatīti āha “atidevabhāvaṃ patto”ti. Yasmā brahmānopi devagatipariyāpannattā devā eva, tasmā vuttaṃ “atibrahmabhāvaṃ patto”ti.

Even though one has attained the state beyond the devas, it is understood that this is a state devoid only of the substrates of defilements and so on, due to the continued existence of the five aggregates as substrates. For that meaning is understood from the condition of existence in another way; thus, it is said ‘attained the state beyond the devas.’ Since even Brahmās, being included within the deva destiny, are themselves devas, therefore it is said ‘attained the state beyond the Brahmās.’

Attānaṃ [M 1.0241] bhāvetvāti sīlādīhi guṇehi attānaṃ vaḍḍhetvā paribrūhitvā ṭhito.

'Having developed oneself' means one is established, having developed and augmented oneself with virtues such as morality.

Puthujjanā tasā taṇhāmānadiṭṭhiparittāsavasena tāsanato. Khīṇāsavā thāvarā nāma sabbaso gatīsu sañcaraṇābhāvato. Tathā hi catunnaṃ saccānaṃ sabbaso adiṭṭhattā bhavadāyajjassa taṇhādāsabyassa bhāvato ekaccāsu gatīsu sañcaraṇasabhāvato sekkhā thāvarā na honti. Bhajamānāti bhajāpiyamānā. Thāvarapakkhameva bhajanti sabbaseṭṭhapakkhaṃ ekantapasaṭṭhaṃ bhajamānabhāvaṃ upādāya.

Ordinary people are 'trembling' because they are frightened by way of the terror of craving, conceit, and wrong views. Those whose taints are destroyed are called 'steadfast' because of the complete absence of wandering among destinies. For, because of not having seen the four truths at all, due to the existence of the inheritance of becoming and of slavery to craving, and due to the nature of wandering in some destinies, trainees are not steadfast. 'Associating' means being caused to associate. They associate only with the steadfast side, the supreme side, by adopting a state of being entirely devoted to that association.

Pahīnakileso khīṇāsavo viseno. Sukhaṃ āyati sukhāyati, tassa kārakaṃ sukhāyatikaṃ.

One who has abandoned defilements, whose taints are destroyed, is 'without the dart.' 'Sukhāyati' means happiness arises; its agent is 'sukhāyatika,' one who brings about happiness.

Brahmadevasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Brahmadeva Sutta is concluded.

4. Bakabrahmasuttavaṇṇanā

4. The Commentary on the Bakabrahma Sutta

175. “Sassato attā ca loko cā”ti evaṃ pavattā diṭṭhi sassatadiṭṭhi. Saha kāyenāti saha tena brahmattabhāvena. Brahmaṭṭhānanti attano brahmavatthuṃ. Aniccaṃ “nicca”nti vadati aniccatāya attano apaññāyamānattā. Thiranti daḷhaṃ, vināsābhāvato sārabhūtanti attho. Uppādavipariṇāmābhāvato sadā vijjamānaṃ. Kevalanti paripuṇṇaṃ. Tenāha “akhaṇḍa”nti. Kevalanti vā jātiādīhi asammissaṃ, virahitanti adhippāyo. Uppādādīnaṃ abhāvato eva acavanadhammaṃ. Koci jāyanako…pe… upapajjanako vā natthi niccabhāvato [V 1.0211] ṭhānena saddhiṃ tannivāsīnaṃ. Niccabhāvañhi so paṭijānāti. Tisso jhānabhūmiyoti dutiyatatiyacatutthajjhānabhūmiyo. Catutthajjhānabhūmivisesā hi asaññasuddhāvāsāruppabhavā. Nibbānanti vā ettha iti-saddo ādiattho, na parisamāpanattho, tasmā “sabba”nti iminā “asañña…pe… bhavā”ti vuttaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Paṭibāhatīti santaṃyeva samānaṃ ajānantova “natthī”ti paṭikkhipati. Eke uttaravihāravāsino.

175. “The self and the world are eternal”—this view, thus arisen, is the eternalist view. “Together with the body” means together with that state of being Brahmā. “The state of Brahmā” refers to one’s own Brahmā-basis. One calls the impermanent “permanent” because its impermanence is not discerned by oneself. “Firm” means strong; the meaning is that it is the essence due to the absence of destruction, that it is substantial. It exists always because there is no arising or change. “Complete” means whole. Therefore, he said, “unbroken.” Or “complete” means unmixed with birth and so forth; the intention is that it is separate. Because there is no arising and so on, it is of a nature not to pass away. Because of the permanent nature of the abode along with its inhabitants, there is no one who is born... or reborn. For he claims permanence. “The three jhāna realms” are the second, third, and fourth jhāna realms. For the special types of the fourth jhāna realm are the non-percipient beings, the Pure Abodes, and the formless realms. Or here, regarding “Nibbāna,” the word “iti” has the sense of “and so on,” not of conclusion; therefore, by this word “all,” it includes what is stated as “the non-percipient... realms.” “Denies” means that, while not knowing what actually exists, one rejects it, saying, “it does not exist.” Some are dwellers in the Northern Monasteries.

Heṭṭhūpapattikoti [M 1.0242] heṭṭhā bhūmīsu uppannaupapattiko. Idāni tamatthaṃ vivarituṃ “anuppanne”tiādi vuttaṃ. Heṭṭhupapattikaṃ katvāti yathāṭhitabhūmito heṭṭhā tatiyajjhānabhūmiyaṃ upapattijhānaṃ katvā, na uparijhānassa viya patthanāmattanti adhippāyo. Paṭhamakāleti tasmiṃ bhave paṭhamakāle. Aññāsi āsannabhāvato. Ubhayanti taṃ taṃ attanā katakammañceva nibbattaṭṭhānañcāti ubhayaṃ. Pamussitvā nibbattiṃ anupadhārento.

“One with a lower birth” means one whose birth has arisen in the lower realms. Now, to explain that meaning, “unarisen” and so forth is said. “Having made a birth below” means having produced the jhāna for rebirth in the third jhāna realm, which is below the realm where one was; the intention is that this is not a mere wish as for a higher jhāna. “At the first time” means at the first time in that existence. “He knew” because of nearness. “Both” refers to both the deed done by oneself and the place where one arose. “Forgetting” means not considering the birth.

Avijjāya gatoti avijjāya saha pavatto. Sahayoge hi idaṃ karaṇavacanaṃ. Tenāha “samannāgato”ti. Aññāṇīti avidvā. Paññācakkhuvirahato andhībhūto, andhabhāvaṃ āpannoti attho. Anāgate saddo hotāyaṃ “vakkhatī”ti yatrasaddapayogena, attho pana vattamānakāliko. Tenāha “bhaṇatī”ti. Tenāha “yatrā”tiādi.

“Gone with ignorance” means proceeded together with ignorance. For this instrumental case is used in the sense of accompaniment. Therefore, he said, “endowed.” “Ignorant” means unknowing. Deprived of the eye of wisdom, he is blind; the meaning is that he has fallen into a state of blindness. The word “vakkhati” (will say) is in the future tense, used with the word “yatra” (where), but its meaning pertains to the present time. Therefore, he said, “bhaṇati” (speaks). Therefore, he said, “where,” and so on.

Maggacoroti maggaparibundhakacoro. Santajjiyamānoti “avijjāgato vata, bho, bako brahmā”tiādinā santajjiyamāno. Satiṃ labhitvāti teneva santajjanena yoniso ummujjitvā purimajātivisayaṃ satiṃ labhitvā. Nippīḷitukāmoti ghaṃsetukāmo dosaṃ dassetukāmo “idaṃ passa yāvañca te aparaddha”nti. Puññakammāti puññakārino. Vedehi ñāṇehi gatattā pavattattā. Antimā brahmupapattīti sabbapacchimā brahmabhāvappatti. Asmābhijappantīti asme abhijappanti. Āyuvaṇṇādivasena brūhitaguṇattā brahmā. Aññehi mahantā brahmā mahābrahmā. Abhibhūti taṃ brahmalokaṃ jeṭṭhakabhāvena abhibhavitvā ṭhito. Anabhibhūtoti aññehi na abhibhūto. Aññadatthūti ekaṃsavacanametaṃ. Dassanavasena daso, sabbaṃ passatīti adhippāyo. Vasavattīti sabbajanaṃ vase vatteti. Issaroti loke issaro. Kattā nimmātāti lokassa kattā nimmātā. Seṭṭho sajitāti ayaṃ lokassa uttamo saṃvibhajitā ca. Vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānanti āciṇṇavasittā vasī, ayaṃ pitā bhūtānaṃ nibbattānaṃ bhabyānaṃ sambhavesīnanti patthenti vikatthenti pihenti mānenti.

“Path-thief” means a thief who robs on the path. “Being threatened” means being intimidated by such things as, “Alas, Baka the Brahmā has gone to ignorance!” “Having regained mindfulness” means having emerged with proper attention from that very threat and regained mindfulness regarding the sphere of a previous birth. “Wishing to crush” means wishing to grind down, wishing to show the fault, thinking, “See how much you have transgressed!” “Those of meritorious deeds” means those who perform meritorious deeds. Because of having gone and proceeded by means of knowledges. “The final Brahmā-birth” means the very last attainment of the state of Brahmā. “They pray to us” means they implore us. Brahmā is so called because his qualities, such as lifespan and beauty, are augmented. Brahmās who are great among others are Mahābrahmās. “The Overcomer” is one who stands having overcome that Brahmā world by virtue of being chief. “Unconquered” means not overcome by others. “Aññadatthu” is a word of certainty. “The Seer” (daso) is so called because of seeing (dassana); the intention is that he sees all. “The Ruler” is one who brings all people under his power. “The Lord” is the master in the world. “The Maker, the Creator” is the maker and creator of the world. “The Chief, the Creator” is the highest in the world and also the apportioner. “The Sovereign, the Father of what has been and what will be”: he is sovereign (vasī) because of his practiced mastery (vasitā); he is the father of beings that have arisen (bhūtānaṃ) and of those that are to be (bhabyānaṃ), that is, of those seeking existence. They long for, boast of, yearn for, and honor him.

Etanti [V 1.0212][M 1.0243] viparītasaññāvasena “idaṃ niccaṃ idaṃ dhuvaṃ idaṃ sassata”ntiādinā vuttaṃ etaṃ appaṃ parittakanti taṃ bhagavā paricchinditvā dasseti. Taṃ pana “ekasmiṃ kosalake tilavāhe vassasate vassasate ekekatiluddhāre kayiramāne tilāni parikkhayaṃ gacchanti, na tveva abbude āyū”ti evaṃ vutto abbudo, taṃvasena vīsatiguṇaṃ nirabbudo, tesaṃ nirabbudānaṃ vasena nirabbudasatasahassaṃ. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthārato pana padume āyuno vassagaṇanā imasmiṃyeva saṃyutte parato āgamissati. Anantadassīti anantassa ñeyyassa anavasesato dassī. Vatasīlavattanti samādānavasena vatabhūtaṃ cārittasīlavasena samāciṇṇattā sīlavattaṃ. Taṃ pana ekamevāti āha “sīlamevā”ti.

“This”: what is said as “this is permanent, this is stable, this is eternal,” and so forth, due to inverted perception. “Is little, is limited”: the Blessed One defines and shows this. Moreover, it is said: “If, from a Kosalan cartload of sesame seeds, one were to remove a single sesame seed every hundred years, the sesame seeds would eventually be exhausted, but not the lifespan in an abbuda.” The abbuda is spoken of thus. By that measure, twenty times that is a nirabbuda; and by the measure of those nirabbudas, one hundred thousand nirabbudas. This is the summary here; but the detailed calculation in years of the lifespan in a paduma will come later in this very Saṃyutta. “Seer of the infinite” means one who sees the infinite knowable in its entirety, without remainder. “Vow and virtuous observance” (vatasīlavattaṃ): it has become a vow (vata) by way of undertaking; it is a virtuous observance (sīlavatta) because it is habitually practiced by way of conduct-virtue. And that is just one thing; thus he said, “virtue alone.”

Apāyesīti ettha yadā so pipāsite manusse pānīyaṃ pāyesi, taṃ samudāgamato paṭṭhāya dassetuṃ “tatrā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Pubbeti purimajātiyaṃ. Esa brahmā “jarāmaraṇassa antaṃ karissāmī”ti ajjhāsayavasena jhānaṃ nibbattetvā brahmaloke nibbatti, so tattha nibbānasaññī ahosi. Jhānaratiyā vītināmetīti tadā tassā kiriyāya avicchedato pavattiṃ upādāya vattamānapayogo. Rattandhakāre purato purato gacchantassa sakaṭassa anussaraṇavasena gacchantānaṃ sakaṭānaṃ nivattanaṃ hotīti “sabbasakaṭāni tatheva nivattitvā”ti vuttaṃ.

Regarding “he gave to drink”: in order to show this, starting from the occurrence when he gave water to thirsty people, the passage beginning “therein” was started. “Formerly” means in a previous birth. This Brahmā, with the intention, “I will make an end to aging and death,” produced jhāna and was reborn in the Brahmā world. There, he had the perception of it as Nibbāna. The present tense in “he spends time delighting in jhāna” is used with reference to the uninterrupted progression of that action at that time. In the darkness of night, the carts that are following turn back by following the lead of the cart going on ahead; thus it is said, “all the carts turned back in that same way.”

Kammasajjāti yuddhasajjā. Vilopanti viluttabhaṇḍaṃ. Eṇikūlasminti ettha “panihatāya niccagaṅgāya nāma”nti keci. “Eṇimigabahulatāya so gaṅgāya tīrappadeso eṇikūlanti vutta”nti apare. Gaṅgeyyakoti gaṅgāsannivāsī.

“Prepared for action” means prepared for battle. “They plunder” (vilopanti): this refers to plundered goods. Regarding “on the Eṇi bank” (eṇikūlasmiṃ): here, some say, “It is the name of the Niccagaṅgā of Panihatā.” Others say, “That region on the bank of the Ganges is called ‘Eṇikūla’ because it is abundant with antelopes.” “A Ganges-dweller” (gaṅgeyyako) means one who lives near the Ganges.

Baddhacaroti paṭibaddhacariyo. Tenāha “antevāsiko”ti. Yasmā buddho sabbaññū, tasmā aññāsi, idha mayhaṃ pamuṭṭhañca sabbaṃ jānāsīti adhippāyo. Sabbaṃ brahmalokaṃ obhāsayanto sabbampimaṃ brahmalokaṃ bhagavā obhāsaṃ abhibhavitvā anaññasādhāraṇaṃ attano obhāsaṃ obhāsento tiṭṭhati.

“One of bound conduct” (baddhacaro) means one whose teacher is followed closely. Therefore, he said, “a pupil.” The intention is: “Because the Buddha is omniscient, therefore he knew; here, you know everything, including what has been forgotten by me.” Illuminating the entire Brahmā world, the Blessed One, having surpassed the light of this entire Brahmā world, stands shining with his own unique radiance.

Bakabrahmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Bakabrahma Sutta is finished.

5. Aññatarabrahmasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Discourse about a Certain Brahmā

176. Tejokasiṇaparikammaṃ [M 1.0244] katvāti “tejokasiṇaparikammajjhānaṃ samāpajjissāmī”ti cittuppādo evettha tejokasiṇaparikammaṃ. Na hi buddhānaṃ aññesaṃ viya tattha jhānasamāpajjanena [V 1.0213] parikammapapañco atthi sabbattheva ciṇṇavasībhāvassa paramukkaṃsabhāvappattattā. Tassa kira brahmuno “yathāhaṃ evaṃ mahānubhāvo añño natthī”ti laddhi, yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – “natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā, yo idha āgaccheyyā”ti. Bhagavā tassa taṃ laddhiṃ vissajjetuṃ tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā tassa upari ākāse nisīdi. Tena vuttaṃ “tejodhātuṃ…pe… tathāgataṃ disvā”ti. Aṭṭhivedhaṃ viyaṃ vijjhitabbo aṭṭhivedhī, yathā aṭṭhiṃ vijjhitvā aṭṭhimiñjaṃ āhacca tiṭṭhati, evaṃ vijjhitabboti attho. Ayaṃ pana aṭṭhivedhī viya aṭṭhivedhī, yathā so laddhiṃ vissajjeti, evaṃ paṭipajjitabboti attho. Sesānanti mahākassapamahākappinaanuruddhattherānaṃ.

176. 'Having performed the preliminary work for the fire kasiṇa' means that the arising of the thought, 'I will attain the absorption of the preliminary work for the fire kasiṇa,' is itself the preliminary work for the fire kasiṇa in this context. For the Buddhas, unlike others, there is no elaboration of preliminary work through attaining absorption, because they have attained the supreme state of complete mastery through practice in all respects. That Brahmā, it seems, had the view, 'There is no other as mighty as I am.' With reference to this, it was said: 'There is no ascetic or brahmin who could come here.' The Blessed One, in order to make him abandon that view, entered the fire element and sat in the sky above him. Therefore it was said: 'Having seen the Tathāgata... in the fire element...' An aṭṭhivedhī is one who is to be pierced like a bone is pierced; the meaning is that just as one pierces a bone and, striking the marrow, stops, so is he to be pierced. This one, however, is to be dealt with like a bone-piercer; the meaning is that one should act in such a way that he abandons his view. 'The others' refers to the Elders Mahākassapa, Mahākappina, and Anuruddha.

Aññabrahmasarīravimānālaṅkārādīnaṃ pabhāti brahmānaṃ sarīrappabhā vimānappabhā alaṅkāravatthādīnaṃ pabhāti imasmiṃ brahmaloke imā sabbā pabhā attano pabhassarabhāvena abhibhavantaṃ. Natthi me sāti idāni me sā diṭṭhi natthi, “natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā, yo idha āgaccheyyā”ti ayaṃ laddhi natthi. Tenāha “tatrāssa…pe… pahīnā”ti. Etthāti etasmiṃ samāgame. Yathā tassa brahmuno sabbaso diṭṭhigataṃ vimuccati dhammacakkhu uppajjati, evaṃ mahantaṃ dhammadesanaṃ desesi.

The radiance of the bodies, celestial mansions, ornaments, and so forth of other Brahmās—that is, the radiance of the Brahmās' bodies, the radiance of their celestial mansions, the radiance of their ornamental objects, and so on—in this Brahmā world, all these radiances he surpasses with his own inherent brilliance. 'I do not have that' means: 'Now that view of mine does not exist; this view, "There is no ascetic or brahmin who could come here," does not exist.' Therefore it was said: 'There, his... was abandoned.' 'Here' means in this assembly. He delivered a great discourse on the Dhamma so that that Brahmā was entirely freed from wrong views and the eye of the Dhamma arose.

“Ajjāpi te, āvuso”tiādinā vuttena tattakeneva. Sarūpena vuttāti paṭhamena pādena catasso, dutiyena ekanti evaṃ pañca abhiññā sarūpena vuttā. Kasmā ettha dibbasotaṃ nāgatanti? Āha “tāsaṃ vasena āgatamevā”ti. Yena imā lokuttarā abhiññā adhigatā, na tassa dibbasotasampādanaṃ bhāriyaṃ paṭipakkhavigamena sukheneva ijjhanato.

By that much stated with 'Even today, friend,' and so forth. 'Stated in their essential form' means that four higher knowledges are stated by the first line, and one by the second, thus five higher knowledges are stated in their essential form. Why is the divine ear not mentioned here? He says: 'It is already included by way of them.' For one by whom these supramundane higher knowledges have been attained, the accomplishment of the divine ear is not difficult, since it is easily accomplished by the removal of opposing factors.

Aññatarabrahmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse about a Certain Brahmā is concluded.

6. Brahmalokasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Brahmaloka Sutta

177. Paccekaṃ [M 1.0245] dvārabāhanti paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ. Pacceka-saddo cettha āvuttivasena veditabbo; “paccekaṃ pacceka”nti āha “ekeko ekeka”nti. Tesu hi eko paccekabrahmā gandhakuṭiyā ekadvārabāhaṃ nissāya ṭhito, aparo aññaṃ. Paccekabrahmāti ca ekacārī brahmā, na parisacārī brahmāti attho. Samiddhi nāma sagge sukhupakaraṇehi, brahmānañca jhānaṃ sukhupakaraṇanti jhānasukhena samiddhoti. Sampattiyā vepullappattatā brahmānañca abhiññāguṇehi vepullappattīti [V 1.0214] āha “phītoti abhiññāpupphehi supupphito”ti. Asahantoti nasahanto narocento.

177. 'Paccekaṃ dvārabāhaṃ' means each door-post. Here, the word 'pacceka' should be understood in the sense of repetition; for 'paccekaṃ paccekaṃ' means 'each one individually.' Among them, one solitary Brahmā stands leaning against one door-post of the perfumed chamber, and another against a different one. And 'paccekabrahmā' means a Brahmā who wanders alone, not a Brahmā who wanders in a retinue. 'Samiddhi' means flourishing in heaven with the requisites for happiness, and for Brahmās, absorption is a requisite for happiness—thus, 'flourishing with the bliss of absorption.' The attainment of greatness for Brahmās is the attainment of greatness through the qualities of higher knowledge—hence it is said: 'Phīto means well adorned with the flowers of higher knowledge.' 'Asahanto' means not enduring, not liking.

Satapadanti satasaddo. Rūpavasenāti rūpasaddavasena, rūpasaddena saddhinti attho. Tathā pantivasenāti etthāpi. Ekacceti eke migārī, tesaṃ byagghīnisārūpakānaṃ pañcasatānīti attho. “Kassa aññassa upaṭṭhānaṃ gamissāmī”ti vimānasampattiyaṃ vimhayakkhiko ahaṅkāravasena vadati. Raṇanti nindanti etehīti raṇā, dosā. Virodhipaccayasannipāte vikāruppatti ruppanaṃ rūpassa pavedhananti āha “sītādīhi ca niccaṃ pavedhita”nti. Sumedho sundarapañño so satthā rūpe na ramati, kiṃ pana mandapañño rūpe saraṇañca pavedhitañca apassanto ramasīti adhippāyo.

'Satapada' means the word 'sata.' 'Rūpavasena' means by way of the word 'rūpa,' meaning connected with the word 'rūpa.' Similarly, 'pantivasena' here too. 'Ekacce' means some hunters, meaning five hundred of them who resemble tigresses. 'Whose attendance shall I seek?'—he speaks with the pride of egotism, being amazed by the attainment of his celestial mansion. 'Raṇa' means faults, because they revile with these. In the arising of opposing conditions, there is change—the breaking up of form is the agitation of form, as he said: 'and constantly agitated by cold and so forth.' Sumedha, the Teacher of lovely wisdom, does not delight in form—how then could a dull-witted person delight in form, not seeing it as a refuge and as agitated? This is the intended meaning.

Brahmalokasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Brahmaloka Sutta is concluded.

7. Kokālikasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Kokālika Sutta

178. Pamāṇakarānaṃ rāgādīnaṃ abhāvato khīṇāsavo rāgādivasena na sakkā imaṃ pamātunti appameyyo, appameyyāni vā cattāri ariyasaccāni vijjhitvā ṭhitattā pamitaṃ pameyyaṃ tassa kato parimeyyo natthi. Tenāha “khīṇāsavo…pe… dīpetī”ti. Tanti khīṇāsavaṃ. Pametuṃ randhagavesī hutvā vajjato paricchindituṃ. Yathāsabhāvato tassa minane nihīnapaññatāya avakujjapaññaṃ.

178. Because of the absence of measuring factors such as lust, the one whose taints are destroyed cannot be measured by way of lust and the like; he is immeasurable. Or, because he stands having pierced the four Noble Truths, which are immeasurable, there is no one who has measured him, no one who can measure him. Therefore it was said: 'The one whose taints are destroyed... illuminates.' 'Him' means the one whose taints are destroyed. To measure him means to seek for flaws and to define him by way of faults. In measuring him according to his true nature, one has an inverted understanding due to inferior wisdom.

Kokālikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Kokālika Sutta is concluded.

8. Katamodakatissasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Katamodaka Tissa Sutta

179. Kiṃ [M 1.0246] kusalagavesitāya “kiṃ kusalaṃ akusala”ntiādinā kinti suṇāti etāyāti kissa vā vuccati paññā.

179. Why is it called wisdom (paññā)? Because with it one listens, inquiring, “What is skillful? What is unskillful?” and so on, in search of the skillful.

Katamodakatissasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Katamodaka Tissa Sutta is concluded.

9. Turūbrahmasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Turūbrahma Sutta

180. Ābādho etassa atthīti ābādhiko. Anantarasutteti anāgatānantare sutte. Varākoti [V 1.0215] anuggahavacanameva, na nippariyāyena vuttavacanaṃ. Piyasīlāti iminā etasmiṃ atthe niruttinayena “pesalā”ti padasiddhīti dasseti. Kabarakkhīnīti byādhibalena paribhinnavaṇṇatāya kabarabhūtāni akkhīni. Yattakanti yaṃ tvaṃ bhagavato vacanaṃ aññathā karosi, tattakaṃ tayā aparaddhaṃ, tassa pamāṇaṃ natthīti attho. Yasmā anāgāmino nāma kāmacchandabyāpādā pahīnā honti, tvañca diṭṭho kāmacchandabyāpādavasena idhāgato, tasmā yāva te idaṃ aparaddhanti ayamevettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

180. 'One who has an illness' is an `ābādhika`. 'In the immediately following sutta' means in the sutta that is immediately subsequent. `Varāko` is merely a term of compassion, not a word used in its literal sense. By 'Piyasīlā', it is shown that the word 'pesalā' is established in this sense by way of etymology. `Kabarakkhīnī` means her eyes had become variegated, their color broken up by the force of illness. `Yattaka` means: 'Inasmuch as you distort the Blessed One’s words, by that much have you transgressed; there is no measure for that.' Since for non-returners sensual desire and ill will are abandoned, and you are seen to have come here driven by sensual desire and ill will, therefore, 'to the extent that you have transgressed'—this is the meaning to be understood here.

Adiṭṭhippattoti appattadiṭṭhinimitto. Gilaviso viya visaṃ gilitvā ṭhito viya. Kuṭhārisadisā mūlapacchindanaṭṭhena. Uttamattheti arahatte. Khīṇāsavoti vadati sunakkhatto viya acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ. Yo aggasāvako viya pasaṃsitabbo khīṇāsavo, taṃ “dussīlo aya”nti yo vā vadati. Samakova vipākoti pasaṃsiyanindā vijjamānaguṇaparidhaṃsanavasena pavattā yāva mahāsāvajjatāya kaṭukataravipākā, tāva nindiyapasaṃsāpi mahāsāvajjatāya samavipākā tattha avijjamānaguṇasamāropanena attano paresaṃ micchāpaṭipattihetubhāvato pasaṃsiyena tassa samabhāvakaraṇato ca. Lokepi hi ayaṃ pure samaṇagārayho hoti, pageva duppaṭipannaduppaṭipannoti samaṃ karontīti.

`Adiṭṭhippatto` means one who has not attained the sign of vision. Like one who has swallowed poison. Like an axe, in the sense of cutting off the root. `Uttamatthe` means in arahantship. He speaks of the one whose taints are destroyed like Sunakkhatta spoke of the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya. The one whose taints are destroyed should be praised like a chief disciple, but someone says of him, 'This one is immoral.' `Samakova vipāko` means: just as blaming one who is praiseworthy—which proceeds by way of destroying his existing qualities—is a very great fault with a most bitter result, so too praising one who is blameworthy has an equal result and is a very great fault. This is because, by superimposing non-existent qualities on him, it becomes a cause for the wrong practice of oneself and others, and because it makes him equal to one who is praiseworthy. For even in the world, this person was formerly reprehensible to ascetics; how much more so when they equate one who has practiced badly with one who has practiced well.

Sakenāti attano sāpateyyena. Ayaṃ appamattako aparādho diṭṭhadhammikattā sappatikārattā ca tassa. Ayaṃ mahantataro kali katūpacitassa samparāyikattā appatikārattā ca.

`Sakena` means by one’s own possession. This is a minor offense, as it pertains to this very life and has a remedy. This is a greater fault, as it is accumulated by one's actions, pertains to the next life, and has no remedy.

“Nirabbudo”ti [M 1.0247] gaṇanāviseso ekoti āha “nirabbudagaṇanāyā”ti, satasahassaṃ nirabbudānanti attho. Nirabbudaparigaṇanaṃ pana heṭṭhā vuttameva. Yamariyagarahī nirayaṃ upetīti ettha yathāvuttaṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ pākatikena ariyūpavādinā vuttanti veditabbaṃ. “Aggasāvakānaṃ pana guṇamahantatāya tatopi ativiya mahantatarā evā”ti vadanti.

“Nirabbuda” is a specific number. He says “one” with the phrase “by the nirabbuda count,” the meaning of which is one hundred thousand nirabbudas. The calculation of a nirabbuda, however, has already been stated below. Here, regarding the phrase “one who reviles the noble ones goes to hell,” the stated lifespan should be understood as what is said for an ordinary person who reviles the noble ones. However, they say, “For the chief disciples, due to the greatness of their virtues, it is even far greater than that.”

Turūbrahmasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Turūbrahma Sutta is concluded.

10. Kokālikasuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Kokālika Sutta

181. Dve kokālikanāmakā bhikkhū, tato idha adhippetaṃ niddhāretvā dassetuṃ – “ko ayaṃ kokāliko”ti? Pucchā. Suttassa aṭṭhuppattiṃ dassetuṃ – “kasmā ca upasaṅkamī”ti? Pucchā[V 1.0216]. Ayaṃ kirātiādi yathākkamaṃ tāsaṃ vissajjanaṃ. Vivekavāsaṃ vasitukāmattā appicchatāya ca mā kassaci…pe… vasiṃsu.

181. There were two monks named Kokālika. Then, to ascertain and show what is intended here, the question is asked: “Who is this Kokālika?” To show the origin of the Sutta, the question is asked: “And why did he approach?” This, beginning with 'indeed,' is the answer to these questions in due order. Because of their desire to live in seclusion and due to their having few wishes, they lived… thinking, “May no one….”

Pakkamissantīti āghātaṃ uppādesi attano icchāvighātanato. Therā bhikkhusaṅghassa niyyādayiṃsu payuttavācāya akatattā therehi ca adīpitattā. Pubbepi…pe… maññeti iminā therānaṃ kohaññe ṭhitabhāvaṃ āsaṅkati avaṇe vaṇaṃ passanto viya, suddhe ādāsatale lekhaṃ uṭṭhāpento viya ca.

Thinking, 'They will depart,' he aroused resentment because his own wish was thwarted. The elders entrusted it to the community of monks; because it was not done with prepared speech and was not declared by the elders. By this phrase, 'Even before... he thinks,' he suspects the elders of being established in hypocrisy, as if seeing a wound where there is none, or as if raising a line on a spotless mirror.

Aparajjhitvāti bhagavato sammukhā “pāpabhikkhū jātā”ti vatvā. Āha “saddhāya ākaro pasādāvaho”ti. Pavattasaddhāyiko vāti atthoti āha “saddhātabbavacano”ti.

“Having offended” means having said in the Blessed One’s presence, “Wicked monks have arisen.” He said, “He is a mine of faith, inspiring confidence.” Or, the meaning is “one who has established faith”; he said, “one whose word is to be believed.”

Pīḷakā nāma bāhirato paṭṭhāya aṭṭhiṃ bhindati, imā pana paṭhamaṃyeva aṭṭhiṃ bhinditvā uggatā. Taruṇabeluvamattiyoti taruṇabillaphalamattiyo. Visagilitoti khittapaharaṇo. Tañca baḷisaṃ visasamaññā loke. “Ārakkhadevatānaṃ sutvā”ti padaṃ ānetvā sambandho.

A boil breaks the bone starting from the outside, but these, having broken the bone first, emerge. “The size of a young beluva fruit” means the size of a young bilva fruit. “Poison-swallowed” means a hurled weapon. And that hook is a term for poison in the world. The phrase “having heard from the guardian deities” is brought in and connected.

Magadharaṭṭhe [M 1.0248] saṃvohārato māgadhako patto, tena. Tilasakaṭaṃ tilavāhāeti vutto. Paccitabbaṭṭhānassāti nirayadukkhena paccitabbapadesassa. Etaṃ “abbudo”ti nāmaṃ.

In the land of Magadha, by common usage, a `māgadhako` is a `patto` (a measure); by that it is measured. “A cart of sesame” is said to be “a cartload of sesame.” “Of the place to be tormented” means of the region to be tormented by the suffering of hell. This is the name “Abbuda.”

Vassagaṇanāti ekato paṭṭhāya dasaguṇitaṃ abbudaāyumhi, tato paraṃ vīsatiguṇaṃ nirabbudādīsu vassagaṇanā veditabbā. Sabbatthāti ababādīsu padumapariyosānesu sabbesu nirayesu. Eseva nayoti heṭṭhimato uparimassa uparimassa vīsatiguṇataṃ atidisati.

“The counting of years”: for the Abbuda lifespan, it is tenfold starting from one; thereafter, the counting of years for Nirabbuda and the others should be understood as twentyfold. “In all cases” means in all the hells, from Ababa and so on, ending with Paduma. “This is the method” extends the twentyfold nature of each higher one from the one below it.

Kokālikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Kokālika Sutta is concluded.

Paṭhamavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the first chapter is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Sanaṅkumārasuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sanaṅkumāra Sutta

182. Porāṇakattāti [V 1.0217] nibbattitvā cirakālattā. Jātattā jano, taṃ ito janeto, tasmiṃ. Khattiyo seṭṭho lokamariyādaparipālanādinā sammāpaṭipattiyaṃ sattānaṃ niyojanena bahukārattā. So hi pare tathā paṭipādento sayampi tattha patiṭṭhitoyeva hotīti seṭṭho vutto. Paṭipakkhavijjhanaṭṭhena pubbenivāsādīnaṃ viditakaraṇaṭṭhena vijjāti. Saddhāhirottappabāhusaccavīriyasatipaññāti ime satta saddhammā. Caranti agatapubbaṃ disaṃ etehīti caraṇāni, sīlādayo pannarasa dhammā.

182. “Because of being ancient” means because of being of long standing after having arisen. “Because of being born, one is a person; in that which generates them.” The Khattiya is the foremost because he is of great help by appointing beings to right practice through protecting the world’s boundaries and so on. For he, while making others practice thus, is himself established in it—thus he is called the foremost. “Knowledge” is so called because it has the characteristic of piercing opponents and of making known past lives, etc. Faith, moral shame, moral dread, great learning, energy, mindfulness, and wisdom—these are the seven good qualities. “Conduct” is so called because with these one travels to a direction not gone to before; they are the fifteen qualities beginning with virtue.

Sanaṅkumārasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sanaṅkumāra Sutta is concluded.

2. Devadattasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Devadatta Sutta

183. Appaññatte eva sikkhāpade chejjagāmikammassa katattā saliṅgeneva ca ṭhitattā “devadatto sāsanato pakkanto”ti na vattabboti acirapakkanteti ettha “sāsanato pakkante”ti avatvā “veḷuvanato [M 1.0249] gayāsīsaṃ gate”ti vuttaṃ. Pakatatto hi bhikkhusaṅghaṃ bhindeyya, na apakatattoti. Vaḷavāyāti vaḷavāya kucchiyaṃ jātaṃ.

183. Because the training rule was not yet laid down, because an act deserving of cutting off had been done, and because he remained with the very sign of a monk, it should not be said, “Devadatta has departed from the Dispensation.” Therefore, regarding the phrase “recently departed,” instead of saying “departed from the Dispensation,” it is said, “he went from Veḷuvana to Gayāsīsa.” For one who is of normal status might split the community of monks, not one who is not of normal status. “Of a mare” means born in the womb of a mare.

Devadattasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Devadatta Sutta is concluded.

3. Andhakavindasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Andhakavinda Sutta

184. Janatanti janānaṃ samūhaṃ, janasañcaraṇaṭṭhānanti attho. Manussānaṃ anupacāreti yattake kasanādikiccaṃ karontānaṃ sañcāro hoti, ettakaṃ atikkamitvā anupacāre. Saṃyojanavippamokkhāti saṃyojanavimokkhahetu. Vivekaratiṃ pavivekasukhajjhānaṃ alabhanto. Cittānurakkhaṇatthanti pubbe maṃ manussā “araññavāsena pavivitto asaṃsaṭṭho āraddhavīriyo”ti maññiṃsu, idāni gāmante vasantaṃ disvā gaṇasaṅgaṇikāya nivuṭṭhoti appasādaṃ āpajjissanti. Yadipi me idha abhirati natthi, evaṃ santepi idheva vasissāmīti vikkhittacittena hutvā na vasitabbaṃ, ko attho cittavasaṃ gantvāti adhippāyo. Satipaṭṭhānaparāyaṇoti [V 1.0218] satipaṭṭhānabhāvanārato. Evaṃ hissa gaṇavāsopi pāsaṃso vivekavāsena vinā samaṇakiccassa asijjhanato.

184. “A crowd” means a group of people; the meaning is a place where people move about. “Out of range of people” means: having gone beyond the range of movement of people doing tasks like ploughing, etc., in a place out of range. “For release from the fetters” means the cause for liberation from fetters. Not obtaining “delight in seclusion,” the jhāna that is the happiness of solitude. “For the sake of protecting the mind” means that previously people thought of me as “one who dwells in the forest, secluded, aloof, energetic,” but now, seeing me living near a village, they will experience displeasure, thinking, “He has become involved in crowds and socializing.” Even though I have no delight here, one should not live with a distracted mind, thinking, “I will live right here.” What is the point of going under the control of the mind? This is the intention. “Devoted to the foundations of mindfulness” means delighting in the development of the foundations of mindfulness. Thus, for him, even dwelling in a group is praiseworthy, because without dwelling in seclusion the task of a recluse is not accomplished.

Vaṭṭabhayato pamutto ajjhāsayavasenāti adhippāyo.

Freed from the fear of the round of rebirth due to the power of his disposition—this is the meaning.

Nisīdi tattha bhikkhūti iminā sattūpaladdhiyā anissitattā yathāruciyā tesaṃ nisajjaṃ dasseti. Tenāha “iminā”tiādi.

By “the monk sat there,” this shows their sitting as they pleased, because of not being dependent on the acquisition of a being. Therefore, it is said, “by this” and so on.

Iminā ca iminā ca ākārena jātanti na anussavadassanametaṃ, na anussavaggahaṇaṃ. Takkahetu nayahetu vā na vadāmīti yojanā. Piṭakaṃ gantho sampadīyati etassāti piṭakasampadānaṃ, ganthassa uggaṇhanato tena piṭakassa uggaṇhanakabhāvena, kenaci ganthānusārena evaṃ na vadāmīti attho. Brahmassa seṭṭhassa dhammassa cariyaṃ vācasikaṃ pavattatīti brahmacariyaṃ, dhammadesanā. Bhāvitena maraṇassa sabbaso bhāgena vippahānena maraṇapariccāgīnaṃ. Te ca khīṇajātikāti āha “khīṇāsavāna”nti.

“Born in this and that manner”—this is not a seeing from oral tradition, nor a grasping from oral tradition. The connection is: “I do not speak based on logic or inference.” “Transmission of the Piṭaka” is that by which the Piṭaka, the text, is transmitted; because of learning the text, by being one who has learned the Piṭaka, the meaning is: “I do not speak thus merely in accordance with some text.” “The holy life” is the verbal conduct of the Dhamma of Brahma, the best, that proceeds; it is the teaching of the Dhamma. For those who have abandoned death through the complete abandonment of death by means of what has been developed. And they are those whose birth is destroyed, thus he says, “of those whose cankers are destroyed.”

Dasadhā [M 1.0250] dasāti dasakkhattuṃ dasa. Aññanti pañcasatādhikasahassato aññaṃ. Puññabhāginoti vivaṭṭanissitapuññassa bhāgino tassā desanāya ettakā sattā jātāti gaṇetuṃ ahaṃ na sakkomīti dasseti. Brahmadhammadesananti brahmunā vuttaṃ āha.

“Tenfold ten” means ten times ten. “Another” means other than the one thousand five hundred. “Partakers of merit” means partakers of the merit that leads to the unfolding. He shows: “I am not able to count how many beings arose from that teaching.” “The teaching of the Brahma-Dhamma” means what was spoken by Brahma.

Andhakavindasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Andhakavinda Sutta is concluded.

4. Aruṇavatīsuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Aruṇavatī Sutta

185. Abhibhū sambhavoti tesaṃ dvinnaṃ mahātherānaṃ nāmāni. Tesaṃ vibhāgaṃ dassetuṃ “tesū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ete dve tassa bhagavato aggasāvakāti dasseti. Avajjhāyantīti heṭṭhā katvā cintenti. Khiyyanti taṃ lāmakato cintetabbataṃ pāpenti pāpakataṃ karonti. Vitthārayantāti tameva lāmakato cintetabbataṃ vepullaṃ pāpentā. Sabbe pāsaṇḍā attano attano samaye siddhante sabbe devamanussā attano attano samaye paṭilābhe paṭiladdhaatthe purisakāraṃ vaṇṇayantīti yojanā.

185. “Abhibhū” and “Sambhava” are the names of those two great elders. To show the distinction between them, “among them” and so forth is stated. It shows that these two are the chief disciples of that Blessed One. “They disparage” means they think of it, having made it low. “They are vexed” means they cause it to reach a state of being thought of as base; they do an evil deed. “They spread it” means they cause that very state of being thought of as base to reach fullness. The connection is as follows: All heretics, in their own respective doctrines, praise human effort; all gods and humans, having attained their goal in their respective attainments, praise human effort.

Ārambhavīriyanti maccusenāsaṅkhātakilesadhunane ārambhavīriyaṃ, yā “ārambhadhātū”ti vuccati[V 1.0219]. Nikkamavīriyanti kosajjapaṭipakkhabhūtaṃ vīriyaṃ, yā “nikkamadhātū”ti vuccati. Payogaṃ karothāti paraṃ paraṃ ṭhānaṃ akkamanato tatopi balavataraṃ bhāvanābhiyogaṃ pavattethāti attho. Tenāha “parakkamathā”ti. Kilesasenā nāma rāgādikilesasamūho, so maraṇapaccayabhāvato “maccuno senā”ti vuccati. Tañhi sandhāya vuttaṃ “mahāsenena maccunā”ti (ma. ni. 3.272, 275, 276). Khandhānaṃ paṭhamābhinibbatti jāti, tadaññaṃ pana tesaṃ paṭipāṭi pavattaṃ saṃsāroti adhippāyenāha “jātiñca saṃsārañcā”ti. Yasmā “ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo”tiādīsu tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhave ādānanikkhepaparicchinnakhandhappavatti “jātī”ti vuccati, sā eva yāva parinibbānā aparāparaṃ pavattamāno saṃsāro “ito cito saṃsaraṇa”nti katvā, tasmā āha “jātisaṅkhātaṃ vā saṃsāra”nti. Paricchedanti pariyosānaṃ. Obhāsaṃ pharīti sambandho. Ālokaṭṭhāneti attanā [M 1.0251] kataālokaṭṭhāne. Ālokakiccaṃ natthīti andhakāraṭṭhāne ālokadassanaṃ viya ālokaṭṭhāne ālokadassanakiccaṃ natthi. Tasmā tesaṃ sattānaṃ “kiṃ āloko ayaṃ, kassa nu kho ayaṃ āloko”ti? Vicinantānaṃ cintentānaṃ. Sabbeti sahassilokadhātuyaṃ sabbe devamanussā. Osaṭāya parisāyāti dhammassavanatthaṃ sabbosaṭāya paricitaparicchinnāya parisāya. Saddaṃ suṇiṃsūti na kevalaṃ saddameva suṇiṃsu, atha kho atthopīti yathādhippeto tesaṃ pakatisavanupacāre viya pākaṭo ahosi, tisahassilokadhātuṃ viññāpesīti.

The effort of beginning (ārambhavīriyaṃ) is the effort in shaking off the mass of defilements counted as the army of death; this is what is called the 'element of beginning' (ārambhadhātu). The effort of exertion (nikkamavīriyaṃ) is the effort that counteracts laziness, known as the 'element of exertion' (nikkamadhātu). 'Apply yourselves' (payogaṃ karotha) means to initiate a stronger and stronger application to meditation, surpassing the previous stage by advancing from one state to the next; hence it is said, 'strive on' (parakkamatha). The army of defilements (kilesasenā) refers to the mass of defilements such as lust, etc., which are called the army of death (maccuno senā) because they are a condition for death. This is referenced in the phrase, 'by the great army of death.' The first arising of the aggregates (khandhānaṃ paṭhamābhinibbatti) is birth (jāti), and their subsequent continuous round is the cycle of existence (saṃsāra), hence it is said, 'birth and the cycle of existence' (jātiñca saṃsārañcā). Since in phrases like 'one birth, two births,' etc., the arising of aggregates, marked by taking up and putting down in each existence, is called 'birth' (jātī), and this very process, continuing repeatedly until final Nibbāna as the cycle of existence (saṃsāro) in its aspect of 'wandering here and there (ito cito saṃsaraṇa),' therefore it is said, 'what is called birth or the cycle of existence' (jātisaṅkhātaṃ vā saṃsāra). 'Limit' (paricchedaṃ) means the end (pariyosānaṃ). 'Pervading with radiance' (obhāsaṃ phari) is the connection. 'In a place of light' (ālokaṭṭhāne) means in a place made into a place of light by oneself. 'There is no function of light' (ālokakiccaṃ natthi) means that just as there is the seeing of light in a dark place, there is no function for seeing light in a place of light. Therefore, for those beings wondering and thinking, 'What is this light? Whose light is this?' 'All' (sabbe) refers to all the gods and humans in the thousandfold world system. 'In an assembled gathering' (osaṭāya parisāya) means in a gathering fully assembled, familiar, and defined for the purpose of hearing the Dhamma. 'They heard the sound' (saddaṃ suṇiṃsu) means not only did they hear the sound, but the meaning also became clear to them as intended, as if in their natural range of hearing, and he made it known throughout the three-thousandfold world system.

Aruṇavatīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Aruṇavatī Sutta is concluded.

5. Parinibbānasuttavaṇṇanā

5. The Commentary on the Parinibbāna Sutta

186. Evaṃ taṃ kusinārāya hotīti yathā anurodhapurassa thūpārāmo dakkhiṇapacchimadisāyaṃ, evaṃ taṃ uyyānaṃ kusinārāya dakkhiṇapacchimadisāyaṃ hoti. Tasmāti yasmā nagaraṃ pavisitukāmā uyyānato upecca vattanti gacchanti etenāti upavattananti vuccati, tasmā. Tanti sālapantibhāvena ṭhitaṃ sālavanaṃ. Antarenāti vemajjhe. Appamajjanaṃ appamādo, so pana atthato ñāṇūpasaṃhitā sati. Yasmā tattha satiyā byāpāro sātisayo, tasmā “satiavippavāsenā”ti vuttaṃ. Appamādapadeyeva pakkhipitvā abhāsi atthato tassa sakalassa buddhavacanassa saṅgaṇhanato.

186. Thus, it is so for Kusinārā: just as the Thūpārāma is to the southwest of Anurādhapura, so too is that park to the southwest of Kusinārā. Therefore, because those who wish to enter the city approach and proceed from the park, it is called Upavattana. Tanti means the sāla grove standing in rows. 'Between' means in the very middle. Heedfulness is non-negligence, which in meaning is mindfulness accompanied by wisdom. Because the activity of mindfulness is pre-eminent there, therefore it is said, 'through unbroken mindfulness.' Having included it in the very term 'heedfulness,' he spoke, since in meaning it encompasses all the Buddha’s teachings by collecting them.

Jhānādīsu citte ca paramukkaṃsagatavasībhāvatāya “ettake kāle ettakā samāpattiyo samāpajjitvā [V 1.0220] parinibbāyissāmī”ti kālaparicchedaṃ katvā samāpattisamāpajjanaṃ parinibbānaparikammanti adhippetaṃ. Theroti anuruddhatthero.

Due to his mastery, which had reached the highest excellence, in the jhānas and other states of mind, having made a determination of time, thinking, 'Having attained this many attainments in this much time, I will attain final Nibbāna,' the attainment of these attainments is understood as the preliminary act for final Nibbāna. 'The Elder' refers to the Elder Anuruddha.

Ayampi cāti yathāvuttapañcasaṭṭhiyā jhānānaṃ samāpannakathāpi saṅkhepakathā eva. Kasmā? Yasmā bhagavā tadā devasikaṃ vaḷañjanasamāpattiyo sabbāpi aparihāpetvā samāpajji evāti dassento “nibbānapuraṃ pavisanto”tiādimāha. Catuvīsati…pe… pavisitvāti ettha keci tāva āhu [M 1.0252] “bhagavā devasikaṃ dvādasakoṭisatasahassakkhattuṃ mahākaruṇāsamāpattiṃ samāpajjati, dvādasakoṭisatasahassakkhattumeva phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjati, tasmā tadāpi catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhā samāpattiyo samāpajjati. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā ‘tathāgataṃ, bhikkhave, arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ dve vitakkā bahulaṃ samudācaranti khemo ca vitakko paviveko ca vitakko’ti (itivu. 38). Khemo hi vitakko bhagavato mahākaruṇāsamāpattiṃ pūretvā ṭhito, pavivekavitakko arahattaphalasamāpattiṃ. Buddhānaṃ hi bhavaṅgaparivāso lahuko matthakappatto samāpattīsu vasībhāvo, tasmā samāpajjanavuṭṭhānāni katipayacittakkhaṇeheva ijjhanti. Pañca rūpāvacarasamāpattiyo catasso arūpasamāpattiyo appamaññāsamāpattiyā saddhiṃ nirodhasamāpatti arahattaphalasamāpatti cāti dvādasetā samāpattiyo bhagavā paccekaṃ divase divase koṭisatasahassakkhattuṃ purebhattaṃ samāpajjati, tathā pacchābhattanti evaṃ catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhā devasikaṃ vaḷañjanakakasiṇasamāpattiyo”ti.

'This too' (Ayampi ca) means that the account of the sixty-five jhānas previously mentioned is also a brief account. Why? Because the Blessed One, without abandoning any of his daily customary attainments, entered them, thus showing, 'Entering the city of Nibbāna,' and so on. 'Twenty-four… entering'—here some say: 'The Blessed One enters the great compassion attainment twelve trillion times daily, and the fruition attainment twelve trillion times as well. Therefore, even at that time, he enters twenty-four trillion attainments. For it was said by the Blessed One: “Two thoughts frequently occur to the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One: the thought of safety and the thought of seclusion” (Itivuttaka 38). The thought of safety is the Blessed One abiding, having fulfilled the great compassion attainment, and the thought of seclusion is the arahant fruition attainment. For the Buddhas, the bhavaṅga state is light, mastery in attainments having reached the summit. Thus, entering and emerging from attainments are accomplished in just a few mind-moments. The five fine-material attainments, the four immaterial attainments, the immeasurable attainment, the cessation attainment, and the arahant fruition attainment—these twelve attainments the Blessed One enters individually a trillion times daily before the meal and likewise after the meal. Thus, there are twenty-four trillion daily customary and kasiṇa attainments.'

Apare panāhu “yaṃ taṃ bhagavatā abhisambodhidivase pacchimayāme paṭiccasamuppādaṅgamukhena paṭilomanayena jarāmaraṇato paṭṭhāya ñāṇaṃ otāretvā anupadadhammavipassanaṃ ārabhantena yathā nāma puriso suviduggaṃ mahāgahanaṃ mahāvanaṃ chindanto antarantarā nisānasilāyaṃ pharasuṃ nisitaṃ karoti, evamevaṃ nisānasilāsadisiyo samāpattiyo antarantarā samāpajjitvā ñāṇassa tikkhavisadabhāvaṃ sampādetuṃ anulomapaṭilomato paccekaṃ paṭiccasamuppādaṅgesu lakkhakoṭisamāpattisamāpajjanavasena sammasanañāṇaṃ pavatteti, tadanusārena bhagavā buddhabhūtopi anulomapaṭilomato paṭiccasamuppādaṅgamukhena vipassanāvasena divase divase lakkhakoṭiphalasamāpattiyo samāpajjati, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, ‘catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasaṅkhā samāpattiyo pavisitvā’”ti.

Others, however, say: 'On the day of his supreme enlightenment, in the last watch of the night, the Blessed One, having directed knowledge back starting from aging and death in reverse order through the factors of dependent origination, began the successive contemplation of phenomena. Just as a man cutting through a very difficult passage, a vast thicket, a great forest, sharpens his axe on a whetstone from time to time, even so, the Blessed One, entering into meditative attainments similar to a whetstone intermittently, perfected the sharpness and clarity of his knowledge by causing the knowledge of comprehension to proceed by way of entering a trillion attainments for each factor of dependent origination in forward and reverse order. Following this, even after becoming a Buddha, the Blessed One daily entered a trillion fruition attainments by way of insight through the factors of dependent origination in forward and reverse order. It is with reference to this that it is said: “Having entered twenty-four trillion attainments.”'

Imāni dvepi samanantarāneva paccavekkhaṇāyapi yebhuyyena nānantariyakatāya jhānapakkhikabhāvato. Yasmā sabbapacchimaṃ bhavaṅgacittaṃ tato tato [M 1.0253] cavanato “cutī”ti vuccati[V 1.0221], tasmā na kevalaṃ ayameva bhagavā, atha kho sabbepi sattā bhavaṅgacitteneva cavantīti dassetuṃ “ye hi kecī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Dukkhasaccenāti dukkhasaccapariyāpannena cuticittena kālaṃ kālakiriyaṃ karonti pāpuṇanti, kālagamanato vā karonti peccāti.

These two are also for immediate reflection, mostly because they are on the side of the jhānas and do not have the nature of an immediate cause. Since the very last life-continuum consciousness, due to ceasing from that state, is called 'death,' therefore, not only this Blessed One, but indeed all beings pass away with the life-continuum consciousness—to show this, it is said, 'whatever beings there are,' etc. 'By the truth of suffering' means: they make an end, attain death, through the death consciousness included within the truth of suffering; or they make an end by passing away, hence 'they die.'

Paṭibhāgapuggalavirahito sīlādiguṇehi asadisatāya sadisapuggalarahito. Saṅkhārā vūpasammanti etthāti vūpasamoti evaṃ saṅkhātaṃ ñātaṃ kathitaṃ nibbānameva sukhanti. Lomahaṃsanakoti lomānaṃ haṭṭhabhāvāpādano. Bhiṃsanakoti avītarāgānaṃ bhayajanako āsi ahosi. Sabbākāravaraguṇūpeteti sabbehi ākāravarehi uttamakāraṇehi sīlādiguṇehi samannāgate. Asaṅkuṭitenāti akuṭitena vipphārikābhāvato. Suvikasitenevāti pītisomanassayogato suṭṭhu vikasitena. Vedanaṃ adhivāsesi sabhāvasamudayādito suṭṭhu paññātattā. Anāvaraṇavimokkho sabbaso nibbidabhāvo. Tenāha “apaññattibhāvūpagamo”ti. Pajjotanibbānasadisoti padīpassa nibbānasadiso tattha vilīyitvā avaṭṭhānābhāvato.

Devoid of counterpart individuals, lacking similar persons due to unmatched virtues like morality, etc. 'Conditioned things subside here'—thus, cessation is known and spoken of as Nibbāna, which is truly bliss. 'Horripilating'—causing the hairs to bristle. 'Terrifying'—it was frightening to those not yet freed from lust. 'Endowed with all excellent qualities'—possessed of all excellent aspects, the highest causes, qualities like morality, etc. 'Uncontracted'—uncontracted because of being expansive. 'Fully blossomed'—well-blossomed due to the union of joy and gladness. 'He endured the feeling'—since it was well-understood from its natural arising, etc. 'The unobstructed liberation'—complete revulsion in every way. Hence it is said, 'approaching the state of non-designation.' 'Like the extinguishing of a lamp'—like the going out of a lamp, since there is no persisting there after dissolving.

Parinibbānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Parinibbāna Sutta is concluded.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Chapter is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

From the Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Brahmasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Clarification of the Hidden Meanings of the Commentary on the Brahma Saṃyutta is concluded.

7. Brāhmaṇasaṃyuttaṃ

7. The Brāhmaṇa Saṃyutta

1. Arahantavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Arahants

1. Dhanañjānīsuttavaṇṇanā

1. Explanation of the Dhanañjānī Sutta.

187. Dhanañjānigottāti [V 1.0222][M 1.0254] ettha pubbapurisato āgatassa kulavaṃsassa nāmābhidhānasaṅkhātaṃ gaṃ tāyatīti gottaṃ. (Kiṃ pana tanti? Aññakulaparamparāsādhāraṇaṃ tassa kulassa ādipurisasamudāgataṃ taṃkulapariyāpannasādhāraṇaṃ sāmaññarūpanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.) Dhanañjānigottaṃ etissanti dhanañjānigottā. Tassā udānassa kāraṇaṃ pucchitvā ādito paṭṭhāya vibhāvetuṃ “so kirā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Nānārasabhojanaṃ detīti yojanā. Pañcagorasasampāditaṃ sālibhattaṃ sūpasākabyañjanaṃ nānārasaṃ brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ. Maṇḍalaggakhagganti maṇḍalaggasaṅkhātaṃ khaggaṃ. Duvidho hi khaggo maṇḍalaggo dīghaggoti. Tattha yassa aggo maṇḍalākārena ṭhito, so maṇḍalaggo. Yassa pana asiputtikā viya dīgho, so dīghaggo.

187. Regarding 'Dhanañjānigottā': here, 'gotta' is the designation of the name of the family lineage that has come from the ancestral line. (But what is that lineage? It should be understood as a general characteristic, not common to the lineage of other clans, but common to those included in that lineage, originating from the founding ancestor.) 'They will have the Dhanañjāni lineage' (Dhanañjānigottaṃ etissanti), hence they are 'Dhanañjānigottā'. Having inquired about the reason for that exclamation, to explain it from the beginning, 'so kirā' and so on is stated. The explanation is that she gives food of various flavors: a brahmin's meal of diverse tastes, which is fine rice prepared with the five products of the cow, with soup, vegetables, and condiments. 'A sword with a rounded tip' (Maṇḍalaggakhagga) means a sword called 'maṇḍalagga'. For there are two kinds of swords: the maṇḍalagga and the dīghagga. Of these, the one whose tip is shaped like a circle is the maṇḍalagga, but the one that is long like a small sword is the dīghagga.

Sāsanāti anusāsanā. “Namo…pe… sambuddhassā”ti evaṃ vuttā pañcapadikagāthā. Satthusāsane hi lokiyacchandaṃ anapekkhitvā esā pañcapadikagāthāti daṭṭhabbā. Okkāvaradharāti pubbapurisasaṅkhātaukkākavaṃsavaradhārikā. Sakkāti sakkuṇeyyaṃ.

'Sāsana' means instruction. "Namo...pe... sambuddhassa"—thus is spoken the five-word verse. Indeed, in the Teacher's dispensation, disregarding worldly meter, this should be seen as the five-word verse. 'Okkāvaradharā' means those who bear the noble lineage of the Okkāka clan, reckoned as ancient ancestors. 'Sakkā' means 'able.'

Evanti “sace me aṅgamaṅgānī”tiādinā iminā pakārena. “Pañca gāthāsatāni pana aṭṭhakathaṃ āruḷhāni, idha pana dve eva uddhaṭā”ti vadanti. Paharituṃ vāti ekavārampi hatthena vā pādena vā paharitumpi parāmasitumpi asakkontoti attho. So hi tassā ariyasāvikāya ānubhāvena attano sāmatthiyena vase vattāpanatthaṃ santajjitvāpi tadanuvattanto nibbiso ahosi. Tenāha “bhotī”tiādi.

'Evaṃ' (thus) means 'in this manner,' as in 'If my limbs,' etc. They say, 'However, five hundred verses are included in the commentary, but here only two are cited.' 'To strike' means that he was unable to strike or even touch her even once with hand or foot. That is the meaning. For he, due to the power of that noble female disciple, even though he had threatened her to bring her under his control by his own strength, remained without power. Therefore, it is said, 'Venerable lady,' etc.

Tassa brāhmaṇassāti attano sāmikabrāhmaṇassa. Upasaṃharantīti upanentī. Tasmiṃ samayeti [V 1.0223] tasmiṃ dukkhuppattikāle “sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā”ti bhagavato [M 1.0255] vacanaṃ anussaritvā “dasabalassa bhagavato”tiādīsu yathāparicitaṃ guṇapadaṃ anussari. Tenāha “dasabalaṃ sarī”ti.

'Of that brahmin' means of her own husband, the brahmin. 'Bringing' means presenting. 'At that time' means at that time when suffering arose, recalling the Blessed One's words, 'All conditioned things are suffering,' she recollected the quality-terms of the Blessed One as she was familiar with them in phrases like 'the Ten-Powered One,' etc. Therefore, it is said, 'remembering the Ten-Powered One.'

Khantisoraccarahitatāya kujjhitvā. Bhijjitvāti saṃyatābhāvato tassa brāhmaṇassa antare mettibhedena bhijjitvā. Evamevāti yathā etarahi akāraṇena, evameva aññadāpi akāraṇenāti attho. Nikkāraṇatādīpane evaṃ-saddo, eva-saddo pana avadhāraṇattho. Nikkāraṇatā ca nāma niratthakatā, niratthakavippalāpabhāvenettha evaṃ-saddassa gahaṇe pavatti gavesitabbā. Garahattho vāyaṃ evaṃ-saddo anekatthattā nipātānaṃ. Garahatthatā cassa vasalisaddasannidhānato pākaṭā eva.

Having become angry due to lack of patience and gentleness. 'Shattered' means that due to the lack of self-restraint, that brahmin's inner mettā was shattered. 'Just so' means that as now without cause, so too at other times without cause. The word 'evaṃ' here indicates causelessness, while the word 'eva' serves to emphasize. Causelessness, indeed, is purposelessness, and in this context, the usage of the word 'evaṃ' should be sought in the sense of purposeless babble. Alternatively, this word 'evaṃ' conveys reproach, as particles can have multiple meanings. And its sense of reproach is evident due to the proximity of the word 'vasali'.

Gāmanigamaraṭṭhapūjitoti iminā gāmanigamaraṭṭhasāmikehi pūjitabhāvo dīpito gāmādīnaṃ tesaṃ vase vattanato. Asukassa nāma puggalassa. Sesanti abhikkantantiādi, yampi caññaṃ idhāgataṃ heṭṭhā vaṇṇitañca.

'Worshipped in villages, towns, and districts'—by this is shown that he was revered by the lords of villages, towns, and districts, because those villages and so on were under their control. 'Of such and such a person'. The rest, such as 'excellent' and so on, and also whatever else has come up here, has been described before.

Dhanañjānīsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dhanañjānī Sutta is concluded.

2. Akkosasuttavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Akkosa Sutta

188. Bhāradvājova soti bhāradvājo nāma eva so brāhmaṇo. Gottavasena hi tayidaṃ nāmaṃ, visesena panetaṃ jātanti dassetuṃ “pañcamattehī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Jānikatāti ñātivaggahānikatā. Pakkho bhinnoti tato eva ñātipakkho naṭṭho. Yathā domanassito anattamanoti vattabbaṃ labhati, evaṃ kupitoti āha “domanassena cā”ti. Dasahīti anavasesapariyādānavasena vuttaṃ pañcahi gāthāsatehi akkosanto tathā akkoseyyāti katvā. Tattha pana yena kenaci akkosantopi akkosatiyeva nāma. Karosi mama bhātikassa pabbajjaṃ.

188. 'Bhāradvājova so' means that brahmin was indeed named Bhāradvāja. Indeed, this is a name based on lineage, but to specifically indicate that it is a birth-name, 'with five hundred,' etc., is stated. 'Jānikatā' means deprived of a group of relatives. 'His faction was broken' means that his faction of relatives was destroyed from that very cause. Just as one might say 'displeased and unhappy,' so too it is said 'angered,' hence 'with displeasure.' 'With ten' is said in the sense of complete exhaustive limit, meaning that he would abuse him as if with five hundred verses. There, however, whoever abuses in any way is indeed abusing. 'You cause my brother's going forth.'

Sambhuñjatīti sambhogaṃ karoti. Akkosādīhi ekato bhuñjati. Vītiharatīti byatihāraṃ karoti, akkosato paccakkosanādinā vinimayaṃ [M 1.0256] karotīti attho. Tenāha “katassa paṭikāraṃ karotī”ti. Assa anussavavasena sutvā “sapati ma”nti saññino bhayaṃ uppajjīti yojanā. Assāti brāhmaṇassa. Sutvāti padaṃ ubhayatthāpi yojetabbaṃ “tavevetaṃ brāhmaṇāti [V 1.0224] sutvā, anussavavasena sutvā”ti ca. Kāmaṃ kisavacchādayo sapanaṃ nādaṃsu, devatānaṃyeva hi so attho, sattānaṃ pana tathā saññā uppannā, sopi tathāsaññī ahosi. Tenāha “anussavavasenā”ti.

'He partakes' means he engages in partaking. He partakes together with abuse and the like. 'He retaliates' means he makes a return, meaning he makes an exchange by abusing in return for abuse, etc. Hence it is said, 'he makes a return for what was done.' The connection is that fear arose in him, who, having heard by hearsay, perceived, 'He curses me.' 'Assa' means of the brahmin. The word 'having heard' should be connected in both places: 'having heard, "This is yours, brahmin,"' and 'having heard by hearsay.' Though Kisa Vaccha and others may not have uttered a curse—for that was indeed the meaning intended by the devas—yet such a perception arose in beings, and he too was of such perception. Hence it is said, 'by hearsay.'

Dantassa sabbaso damathaṃ upagatattā. Nibbisevanassāti rāgadosādihetukavipphandanarahitassa. Tassevāti paṭikujjhantasseva puggalassa tena kodhena pāpaṃ hoti pāpassa santānantarasaṅkantiyā abhāvato. Keci pana “tassevāti tasseva paṭikujjhantapurisassa tena paṭikujjhanena. Pāpiyoti paṭikujjhantapuggalassa lāmakataro”ti evamettha atthaṃ vadanti. Satiyā samannāgato hutvā paṭisaṅkhāne ṭhito adhivāseti, na saho mūḷho hutvāti adhippāyo. Ubhinnaṃ tikicchantanti ubhinnaṃ uppannakodhasaṅkhātaṃ kilesabyādhiṃ tikicchantaṃ vūpasamentaṃ taṃ puggalaṃ. Yo puggalotiādinā purimāsu gāthāsu pavattitāni padāni sambandhitvā dasseti. Pañcasu khandhesu yāthāvato vinītā ariyadhammassa kovidā nāma hontīti āha “dhammassāti pañcakkhandhadhammassā”ti. Idāni tamatthaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ katvā dassento āha “catusaccadhammassa vā”ti.

To one who is fully tamed, because of having attained complete self-control. 'Nibbisevanassa' means devoid of agitation caused by lust, hatred, and the like. 'To him alone' means that for the very person who retaliates, that anger brings harm—because there is no transfer of the continuity of evil. Some, however, explain the meaning here thus: ''Tasseva' (to him alone) means to the very person who retaliates, by that retaliation. 'Pāpiyo' (worse) means that the retaliating individual becomes even more inferior.' The meaning is that, endowed with mindfulness, established in reflection, he endures, not overcome and bewildered. 'Healing both' refers to that person who cures and pacifies the defilement-sickness called anger that has arisen in both. It shows the words that occurred in the previous verses, connecting them with 'that person,' etc. He says that those who are truly disciplined in the five aggregates are called 'skilled in the noble Dhamma,' thus: ''Dhamma' means the Dhamma of the five aggregates.' Now, fully explaining that meaning, he says, 'or in the Dhamma of the four truths.'

Akkosasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Akkosa Sutta is concluded.

3. Asurindakasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Asurindaka Sutta

189. Tenevāti bhātupabbajiteneva. Assevāti titikkhassa. “Taṃ jayaṃ hotī”ti liṅgavipallāsavasena vuttanti āha “so jayo hotī”ti, dujjayaṃ kodhaṃ titikkhāya jinantassāti adhippāyo. Yasmā titikkhādayo na kodhavasikaṃ dhuraṃ, taṃ pana bālānaṃ maññanāmattanti [M 1.0257] idha imamatthaṃ vibhāvetuṃ “katamassā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vijānatova jayo na avijānato titikkhāya abhāvato. Na hi avijānanto andhabālo kodhaṃ vijetuṃ sakkoti. Kevalaṃ jayaṃ maññati kilesehi parājito samānopīti adhippāyo.

189. ‘By him’ means by the brother who has gone forth. ‘Of him’ means of one with forbearance. ‘That victory is his’ is stated by way of a gender reversal; thus he said ‘so victory is his,’ the meaning being for one who conquers hard-to-conquer anger through forbearance. Since forbearance and so on are not a burden subject to anger, but that is merely the conceiving of fools, therefore ‘of what sort’ and so on is said here to explain this meaning. Victory belongs to one who knows, not to one who does not know, due to the absence of forbearance. For an ignorant, blind fool cannot conquer anger. He merely thinks he has victory, though he is defeated by the defilements—this is the meaning.

Asurindakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Asurindaka Sutta is concluded.

4. Bilaṅgikasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Bilaṅgika Sutta

190. Suddhanti kevalaṃ sambhāravirahitaṃ. Sambhārayuttanti kaṭukabhaṇḍādisambhārasahitaṃ. Kañjito nibbattattā kañjikaṃ, āranālaṃ, bilaṅganti attho. Nāmaṃ gahitaṃ saṅgītikāle “bilaṅgikabhāradvājo”ti [V 1.0225] visesanavasena. Tayoti dhanañjāniyā sāmiko bhāradvājo, akkosakabhāradvājo, asundarikabhāradvājoti ādito tīsu suttesu āgatā tayo. Meti mayhaṃ.

190. ‘Plain’ means simply, devoid of ingredients. ‘With ingredients’ means accompanied by ingredients such as bitter condiments and the like. Because it is produced from fermented gruel it is called ‘kañjikaṃ,’ that is, sour gruel or ‘bilaṅga.’ The name was taken up at the time of the council as ‘Bilaṅgika Bhāradvāja’ by way of specification. ‘Three’ refers to the three who appear in the first three suttas: Dhanañjānī’s husband Bhāradvāja, Akkosaka Bhāradvāja, and Asundarika Bhāradvāja. ‘Me’ means my.

Bilaṅgikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Bilaṅgika Sutta is concluded.

5. Ahiṃsakasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Ahiṃsaka Sutta

191. Esāti brāhmaṇo. “Ahiṃsako aha”nti tadatthaṃ sādhetuṃ icchāya kathesīti vuttaṃ “ahiṃsakapañhaṃ pucchī”ti. Tathā ce assāti yathā te nāmassa attho, tathā cetaṃ bhaveyyāsi anvatthanāmako bhaveyyāsi ahiṃsako eva siyāti. Na dukkhāpeti dukkhamattampi na uppādeti, dukkhato apanetīti attho.

191. ‘This one’ means the brahmin. Wishing to establish the meaning of ‘I am non-violent,’ he spoke—thus, it is said, ‘he asked the question about non-violence.’ ‘And if it were so’ means: may you be as the meaning of your name is, may you be one whose name is true to its meaning, may you indeed be non-violent. ‘He does not cause suffering’ means he does not produce even a measure of suffering; the meaning is, he removes one from suffering.

Ahiṃsakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Ahiṃsaka Sutta is concluded.

6. Jaṭāsuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Jaṭā Sutta

192. Jaṭāpañhassāti “antojaṭā bahijaṭā”ti evaṃ jaṭāpariyāyassa pañhassa.

192. ‘Of the question on entanglement’ means of the question concerning the category of entanglement, as in ‘internal entanglement, external entanglement.’

Jaṭāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Jaṭā Sutta is concluded.

7. Suddhikasuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Suddhika Sutta

193. Suddhikapañhassāti [M 1.0258] “nābrāhmaṇo sujjhatī”ti evaṃ suddhasannissitassa pañhassa. Sīlasampannoti pañcavidhaniyamalakkhaṇena sīlena samannāgato. Tapokammanti anasanapañcātapatappanādiparibhedanatapokammaṃ karontopi. Vijjāti tayo vedāti vadanti “tāya idhalokatthaṃ paralokatthaṃ ñāyantī”ti katvā. Gottacaraṇanti gottasaṅkhātaṃ caraṇaṃ. Brāhmaṇo sujjhati jeṭṭhajātikattā. Tathā hi so eva tapaṃ ācarituṃ labhati, na itaro. Aññā lāmikā pajāti itaravaṇṇaṃ vadati. Vacanasahassampīti gāthānekasahassampi. Anto kilesehi pūtiko sabhāvena pūtiko. Kiliṭṭhehi kāyakammādīhi kāyaduccaritādīhi.

193. ‘Of the question on purity’ means of the question connected with purity, as in ‘a non-brahmin is not purified.’ ‘Endowed with virtue’ means possessed of virtue characterized by the five kinds of restraint. ‘Austere practice’ means while also performing the austere practice of mortification, which is divided into fasting, enduring the five fires, and so on. ‘Knowledge’ refers to what they call the three Vedas, on the grounds that ‘through them, this world and the next world are known.’ ‘Lineage and conduct’ means conduct designated as lineage. A brahmin is purified due to being of the highest birth. For he alone is permitted to practice austerity, not another. ‘Other inferior folk’ refers to the other classes. ‘Even a thousand utterances’ means even many thousands of verses. ‘Rotten within’ means putrid with defilements, putrid by nature. ‘By defiled things’ means by bodily actions and so on, that is, by bodily misconduct and so on.

Suddhikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Suddhika Sutta is concluded.

8. Aggikasuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Aggika Sutta

194. Aggiparicaraṇavasenāti [V 1.0226] aggihuttajuhanavasena. Sannihitoti missībhāvaṃ sampāpito. Tathābhūto ca so sappinā saddhiṃ yojito nāma hotīti āha “saṃyojito”ti. Apāyamaggaṃ okkamati micchādiṭṭhimicchāsaṅkappādīnaṃ attano santāne samuppādanato. Tenāha “imaṃ laddhi”ntiādi.

194. ‘By way of tending the fire’ means by way of fire oblation and sacrifice. ‘Brought together’ means brought into a state of being mixed. And being so, it is indeed yoked with ghee; hence it is said, ‘conjoined.’ He enters the path to ruin due to arousing wrong view, wrong intention, and so on, in his own mental continuum. Therefore he says, ‘this doctrine,’ and so on.

Jātiyāti sadosakiriyāparādhassa asambhavena parisuddhāya jātiyā. Nānappakāre aṭṭhārasavijjāṭṭhānasaññite ganthe. Sutavāti sutvā niṭṭhaṃ patto aggadakkhiṇeyyattāti adhippāyo.

‘By birth’ means by a birth that is purified due to the impossibility of faulty action and offense. ‘In various kinds’ refers to the texts designated as the eighteen branches of knowledge. ‘Learned’ means one who, having heard, has reached the culmination; the meaning is that he is the foremost worthy of offerings.

Pubbenivāsañāṇenāti idaṃ loke sāsane ca niruḷhatāvasena vuttaṃ. Aññe hi pubbenivāsaṃ jānantā pubbenivāsañāṇeneva jānanti, bhagavā pana sabbaññutaññāṇenapi jānāti. Dibbena cakkhunāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Sabbaso jāti khīyati etenāti jātikkhayo, aggamaggo[M 1.0259], tena pattabbattā āpannattā ca jātikkhayo arahattaṃ. Jānitvā vositavosānoti vijānitabbaṃ catusaccadhammaṃ maggañāṇena jānitvā soḷasannampi kiccānaṃ vositavosāno.

‘By the knowledge of past abodes’ is stated here in terms of what is conventional in the world and in the Dispensation. For others who know past abodes know them only through the knowledge of past abodes; but the Blessed One knows them also through the knowledge of omniscience. ‘With the divine eye’—here too, the same principle applies. ‘By this, birth is altogether destroyed’—that is the destruction of birth, the supreme path. Because it is to be attained by that path and because it has been attained, the destruction of birth is arahantship. ‘Having known, having completed what is to be completed’ means having known with path-knowledge the Dhamma of the Four Truths which is to be known, one has completed the completion of all sixteen duties.

Uppattiṃ dīpetvāti pāyasadānassa āgamanaṃ pakāsetvā. Gāthāhi abhigītanti dvīhi gāthāhi mayā abhigītaṃ. Abhuñjitabbanti bhuñjituṃ na yuttaṃ. “Abhojaneyya”nti kasmā vuttaṃ, nanu bhagavato ajjhāsayo accantameva suddhoti? Saccametaṃ, brāhmaṇo pana pubbe adātukāmo pacchā gāthā sutvā dhammadesanāya muduhadayo hutvā dātukāmo ahosi, tasmā taṃ bhikkhūnaṃ anāgate diṭṭhānugatiāpajjanatthaṃ paṭikkhipi. Tathā hi anantarasutte kasibhāradvājasutte ca evameva paṭipajji. Tenāha “tvaṃ brāhmaṇā”tiādi. Kilañjamhi…pe… pakāsitāti etena gāthaṃ uddesaṭṭhāneva ṭhapetvā bhagavā brāhmaṇassa vitthārena dhammaṃ desesīti dasseti. Gāyanenāti gāyanakena, gānena vā. Atthañca dhammañcāti sadevakassa lokassa hitañceva tassa kāraṇañca. Sampassantānanti sammadeva passantānaṃ. Dhammoti paveṇiāgato cārittadhammo na hoti. Bhojanesu ukkaṃsagataṃ dassetuṃ “sudhābhojana”nti āha. Dhamme satīti ariyānaṃ ācāradhamme sati taṃ ālambitvā jīvantānaṃ etadeva seṭṭhanti “somaṃ bhuñjeyya pāyasa”nti taṃ ārabbha kathāya uppannattā.

‘Having explained the origin’ means having clarified the arrival of the milk-rice offering. ‘Sung in verses’ means sung by me in two verses. ‘Not to be eaten’ means it was not proper to eat. ‘Why was it said to be “unfit for eating”? Was not the Blessed One’s intention utterly pure?’ Indeed, it was. But the brahmin, initially unwilling to give, later, upon hearing the verses and the Dhamma teaching, became soft-hearted and wished to give. Therefore, the Buddha rejected it to prevent future monks from falling into imitation. For in the immediately following sutta, the Kasibhāradvāja Sutta, he acted in the very same way. Hence, it is said, ‘You, brahmin…’ and so on. By ‘In the Kilañja…until…was made clear,’ it is shown that, having stated the verse merely as a topic, the Blessed One expounded the Dhamma in detail to the brahmin. ‘By singing’ means by a singer, or by a song. ‘And meaning and Dhamma’ means the welfare of the world with its gods and the cause of that welfare. ‘Of those who see’ means of those who see rightly. ‘Dhamma’ means it is not the customary, traditional Dhamma. To show its excellence among foods, he said, ‘ambrosial food.’ ‘When the Dhamma exists’ means when the Dhamma of the conduct of the noble ones exists, this alone is best for those who live relying on it. Because the discussion arose concerning that, it is said, ‘one should partake of the soma-like milk-rice.’

Sallakkheti ayaṃ brāhmaṇo. Sesā paccayā niddosā te ārabbha kathāya appavattitattā. Kukkuccavūpasantanti [V 1.0227] aggiāhitapadassa viya saddasiddhi veditabbā. Annena pānenāti lakkhaṇavacanametaṃ yathā “kākehi sappi rakkhitabba”nti. Tenāha “desanāmattameta”nti. Bahusassaphaladāyakaṃ sukhettaṃ viya paṭiyattanti sammā kasanabījanaudakānayanāpanayanādinā susajjitaṃ khettaṃ viya sīlādiguṇavisesasampādanena paṭiyattaṃ puññakkhettaṃ etaṃ.

This brahmin considers. The remaining requisites are faultless, since no discussion arose concerning them. ‘One whose remorse is calmed’ should be understood as a word formation, just like the word ‘aggiāhita.’ ‘With food and drink’ is a characteristic expression, just as it is said, ‘Ghee should be guarded from crows.’ Therefore it is said, ‘This is merely a designation.’ ‘Prepared like a fertile field yielding abundant grain and fruit’ means this field of merit is prepared through the cultivation of special qualities like virtue, just as a field is well-prepared by means of proper plowing, sowing, irrigation, drainage, and so on.

Aggikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Aggika Sutta is concluded.

9. Sundarikasuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Sundarika Sutta

195. Ānetvā [M 1.0260] hunitabbato āhuti. Sappimadhupāyasādīhi aggiṃ juhoti etthāti aggihuttaṃ, sādhiṭṭhānaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tenāha “agyāyatana”ntiādi. Suvisodhito cassāti nihīnajātikānaṃ anena suṭṭhu visodhito ca bhaveyya. “Me”ti padaṃ ānetvā sambandho.

195. An ‘āhuti’ is so called because it is to be brought and offered. An ‘aggihutta’ is so called because one offers to the fire with ghee, honey, milk-rice, and so forth; this should be understood as having a location. Therefore it is said, 'the place of fire,' and so on. ‘He might be well purified’ means that by this, one of low birth might be well purified. The word 'me' should be brought in to establish the connection.

Aphalaṃ karotīti ito paṭṭhāya yāva demīti padaṃ. Tāva anantarasuttavaṇṇanāya āgatasadisamevāti peyyālavasena ṭhapesi, na sappisaṅkhāraṭṭhapanaṃ. Himapātassa ca sītavātassa ca paṭibāhanatthanti akāraṇametanti taṃ anādiyitvā aññameva sukāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ “paṭibalovā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sañjānitvāti “nāyaṃ brāhmaṇo”ti sañjānitvā.

From 'he renders fruitless' up to the word 'I give,' the passage is placed by way of abbreviation, as it is similar to what is found in the commentary on the immediately preceding sutta; it is not the placing of the section on the preparation of ghee. Regarding the warding off of snowfall and cold winds, considering this to be an invalid reason and disregarding it, another valid reason is shown: 'he is capable,' and so on. 'Having recognized' means having recognized, 'This is not a brahmin.'

Nīcakesantanti rassakesantaṃ. Brāhmaṇānaṃ suddhiatthā sikhāti āha “pavattamattampi, sikhaṃ adisvā”ti, “paramahaṃsaparikkhādinā”ti keci.

'Nīcakesantaṃ' means 'rassakesantaṃ' (short hair). For the sake of purity, the brahmins say of the top-knot, 'even just what is present, without a visible top-knot.' Some say, '[it is defined] by the paring of the paramahaṃsa wanderers.'

Akāraṇaṃ dakkhiṇeyyabhāvassa jāti adakkhiṇeyyabhāvahetūnaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ apaṭikkhepabhāvato. Etanti sīlādibhedaṃ caraṇaṃ. Dakkhiṇeyyabhāvassa kāraṇaṃ adakkhiṇeyyabhāvakārakapāpadhammānaṃ tadaṅgādivasena pajahanato. Assāti brāhmaṇassa. Tamatthanti taṃ dakkhiṇeyyabhāvassa kāraṇatāsaṅkhātamatthaṃ upamāya vibhāvento. Sālādikaṭṭhā jātovāti sālādivisuddhakaṭṭhāva jāto. Sāpānadoṇiādiavisuddhakaṭṭhā jāto aggikiccaṃ na ca na karoti. Evanti yathā aggi yato kutoci jātopi aggikiccaṃ karotiyeva, evaṃ caṇḍālakulādīsu jātopi dakkhiṇeyyo na na hoti guṇasampadāvasena ariyānaṃ vaṃse pajātattāti āha “guṇasampattiyā jātimā”ti. Dhitiyā guṇasampattiyā pamukhabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “so hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha dhitiyāti vīriyena. Tañhi anuppannānaṃ kusaladhammānaṃ uppādanaparibrūhanehi te dhāreti. Hiriyā dose nisedheti, sammadeva pāpānaṃ jigucchane sati tesaṃ pavattiyā avasaro eva [V 1.0228] natthi. Monadhammena ñāṇasaṅkhātena ottappadhammena. Kāraṇākāraṇajānanakoti tesaṃ tesaṃ [M 1.0261] dhammānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ṭhānaṃ, pāpadhammānaṃ vā vippakārasabhāvaṭṭhānaṃ jānanako.

Birth is not the cause of being worthy of offerings, because of the non-rejection of evil states which are the cause of unworthiness. This refers to conduct, distinguished as virtue and so forth. The reason for being worthy of offerings is the abandonment, by way of substitution and so forth, of the evil qualities that cause unworthiness. 'Assa' refers to a brahmin. 'That purpose' means explaining that purpose, designated as the cause of being worthy of offerings, by means of a simile. 'Or born from wood such as sālā' means born from pure wood such as sālā. Born from impure wood such as a dog's trough, fire certainly does not fail to perform its function. Thus, just as fire, wherever it arises, performs its function, so too, even if born in a family of outcastes, one does not fail to be worthy of offerings due to the possession of virtues, being born in the lineage of the noble ones. Hence it is said, 'one of noble birth through the attainment of virtues.' To show the foremost position of fortitude among the attainments of virtue, it is said, 'so hī' and so on. Therein, 'dhitiyā' means 'by energy.' For it upholds them through the arising and development of wholesome qualities not yet arisen. Through moral shame, one prevents faults; for when there is proper disgust toward evil, there is no opportunity at all for its occurrence. Through the quality of a sage, which is designated as knowledge; through the quality of moral dread. 'One who knows cause and non-cause' is one who knows the true condition of those various phenomena, or the condition of the adverse nature of evil states.

Paramatthasaccena nibbānena ārammaṇapaccayabhūtena ariyamaggena danto. Indriyadamenāti tato eva ariyena indriyasaṃvarena upagato. Vidanti tehi saccānīti vedā. Maggavedānaṃ antanti ariyaphalaṃ. Kilesānaṃ antanti tesaṃ anuppādanirodhaṭṭhānaṃ. Yaññoti aggaphalaṃ. Niratthakanti aphalaṃ tesaṃ anāgamanato, āgatānampi aggadakkhiṇeyyābhāvato. Juhati deti.

Tamed by the noble path, which has as its object-condition Nibbāna, the ultimate truth. 'Indriyadamena' (by restraint of the faculties) means endowed with the noble restraint of the senses arising therefrom. The Vedas are so called because 'by them, they know the truths.' 'The end of the path-knowledges' is the noble fruit. 'The end of the defilements' is the state of their non-arising and cessation. 'Yañña' (sacrifice) means the highest fruit. 'Niratthaka' (fruitless) means it is without fruit because of their non-coming, and even for those who have come, because of the absence of a supreme one worthy of offerings. 'Juhati' means 'deti' (he gives).

Suyiṭṭhanti sudānaṃ aggadakkhiṇeyyalābhena. Suhutanti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Atha vā suyiṭṭhanti suṭṭhu sammadeva yiṭṭhaṃ sāre upanītaṃ mama idaṃ deyyavatthu. Suhutanti etthāpi eseva nayo.

'Suyiṭṭha' (well-sacrificed) means a good gift due to gaining a supreme one worthy of offerings. 'Suhuta' (well-offered) is a synonym for the same. Alternatively, 'suyiṭṭha' means: 'this gift of mine has been well and rightly sacrificed, brought to its essence.' The same principle applies to 'suhuta' here as well.

Upahaṭamatteti brāhmaṇena “bhuñjatu bhava”nti upanītamatte. Nibbattitojamevāti savatthukaṃ aggahetvā vatthuto vivecitaojameva. Tena taṃ sukhumattaṃ gatanti taṃ habyasesaṃ sabbaso sukhumabhāvaṃ gatanti ojāya anoḷārikatāya purimākāreneva paññāyamānataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, na pana ojāya eva kevalāya gahaṇaṃ sandhāya. Sā hi avinibbhogavuttitāya visuṃ gaṇhituṃ na sakkā, tasmā devatāhipi savatthukā gayhati. Manussānaṃ vatthūti karajakāyamāha. Oḷārikavatthutāya devānaṃ viya gahaṇī na tikkhāti dibbojasammissatāya sammā pariṇāmaṃ na gacchati.
