Ariyānaṃ adhicittaadhipaññāsikkhā viya adhisīlasikkhāpi sabbā ativiya kantā evāti āha “kiñcāpī”tiādi. Imasmiṃ panattheti imasmiṃ sotāpannassa bhavasaṅkhāte atthe niddhāretvā vuccamāne. Pañcasīlampi yasmā diṭṭhi viya bhavantarepi appahīnaṃ.

"Maggenāgatā" means they have arrived or arisen through the attainment of the path. "Ariyakantasīla" means the virtuous conduct that is pleasing, agreeable, and delightful to the noble ones. Just as the training in higher mind and higher wisdom is exceedingly pleasing to the noble ones, so too is all the training in higher virtue—thus it is said, "even though," and so on. "In this context" means when this matter, designated as existence for a stream-enterer, is being determined and explained. The five precepts also, since like wrong view, are not abandoned even in another existence.

Daliddasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dalidda Sutta is concluded.

5. Rāmaṇeyyakasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Rāmaṇeyyaka Sutta

261. Āramanti ettha sattāti ārāmā, manoramā upavanādayo. Te eva cetenti ettha saddhāya attano pītisomanassaṃ sandhahantīti cetiyāti ca vuccanti. Manussaramaṇīyabhāvassāti manussānaṃ āramaṇīyabhāvassa. Tassa pana sīlādiguṇavasena acinteyyāparimeyyānubhāvatāpi hotīti bhagavā “nāgghanti soḷasi”nti avoca. Acetanāya bhūmiyā ramaṇīyatā nāma guṇavisiṭṭhānaṃ ariyānaṃ sevanavasena veditabbāti vuttaṃ “idāni…pe… gāme vātiādimāhā”ti.

261. "Ārāma" means places where beings delight; these are delightful groves and parks. Because beings, with faith, establish their joy and gladness there, they are also called "cetiyas." "Of the state of being delightful for humans" means of the state of being a resort for humans. But because of its inconceivable and immeasurable power due to qualities such as virtue, the Blessed One said, "They are not worth a sixteenth part." The delightfulness of inanimate ground should be understood as due to association with noble ones distinguished by their virtues, as stated in the passage beginning "Now... in a village or..." and so on.

Rāmaṇeyyakasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Rāmaṇeyyaka Sutta is concluded.

6. Yajamānasuttavaṇṇanā

6. Commentary on the Yajamāna Sutta

262. Yajantānanti dakkhiṇeyyaṃ uddissa dentānaṃ. Aṭṭhuppattiko suttanikkhepoti dassetvā atthavaṇṇanaṃ kātuṃ “tadā kirā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Agganti seṭṭhaṃ. Tehi tehi vā yathāladdhasappiādayo mā nassantu, aggabhāvena gahitāni sappiādīni kevalaṃ aggimhi jhāpanena, devā [M 1.0340] manussā micchāgāhena mā nassantu. Takkenāti takkamattena. “Kathemā”ti amhe maññatha, idāni passatha, paccakkhato ayaṃ vo…pe… āgacchatīti āhaṃsūti yojanā.

262. "Yajantānaṃ" means of those who give, having designated a worthy recipient. Having shown that the exposition of the sutta has an occasion of arising, the explanation of the meaning begins with "At that time, indeed..." "Agga" means the best. Let not the ghee and other things obtained by them in various ways perish; let not the ghee and other offerings, taken as the best, perish merely by being burnt in the fire; let not gods and humans perish through wrong views. "Takkena" means merely by reasoning. "'Kathemā' means 'you think of us'; now see for yourselves, this one comes to you directly... they said"—this is the connection.

Upadhivipākanti [V 1.0298] upadhīsu vā vipaccati, upadhayo vā vipākā etassāti upadhivipākaṃ. Vipphāravantaṃ hoti vipulapakkhatāya. Bhikkhusaṅghassa adaṃsu “sammāsambuddhena mahābrahmunā ca evaṃ ovādo dinno”ti.

"Upadhivipāka" means either it ripens in the substrata of existence, or the substrata are its result. It is extensive due to its vastness. They gave to the community of monks, saying, "Thus was the advice given by the Perfectly Enlightened One and by Mahābrahmā."

Yajamānasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Yajamāna Sutta is concluded.

7. Buddhavandanāsuttavaṇṇanā

7. Commentary on the Buddhavandanā Sutta

263. Uṭṭhahāti uṭṭhānaṃ kāyikavīriyaṃ karohi. Tenāha “vicara, loke”ti. Cetasikavīriyaṃ pana bhagavatā matthakaṃ pāpitameva. Tenāha “vijitasaṅgāmā”ti. Dvādasayojanikassa uccabhāvena. Vitthārato pana āyāmato ca anekayojanasatasahassaparimāṇacakkavāḷaṃ atibyāpetvā ṭhitassa. Pannabhārāti pātitabhāra. Nikkhepitabbato bhārāti āha “oropitakhandhā”tiādi. Te hi taṃsamaṅgino puggalassa sampātanaṭṭhena bhārā nāma. Vuttañhetaṃ “bhārā have pañcakkhandhā”ti (saṃ. ni. 3.22). Tadekadesā ca kilesābhisaṅkhārā. Pannarasāya puṇṇamāya rattinti yathā pannarasapuṇṇamāya rattiyaṃ paripuṇṇakāle upakkilesavimutto cando sobhati, evaṃ tava cittaṃ sabbaso upakkilesavimuttaṃ sobhatīti adhippāyo.

263. "Uṭṭhahāti" means: "Make an effort, physical energy." Therefore, he said, "Wander in the world." But mental energy was indeed brought to its peak by the Blessed One. Therefore, he said, "Victorious in battle." Due to his height of twelve yojanas. And of him who stood pervading the world-system measuring many hundreds of thousands of yojanas in breadth and in length. "Pannabhāra" means one who has dropped the burden. "A burden because it is to be laid down," thus he said, "one who has put down the aggregates," and so on. For they are called burdens for a person endowed with them in the sense of causing downfall. And this was said: "The five aggregates, indeed, are burdens." The defilements and formations are a part of that. "On the fifteenth full-moon night" means: just as on the fifteenth full-moon night, at the time of its fullness, the moon, freed from blemishes, shines, so too your mind, completely freed from blemishes, shines—this is the intention.

Buddhavandanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Buddhavandanā Sutta is concluded.

8. Gahaṭṭhavandanāsuttavaṇṇanā

8. Commentary on the Gahaṭṭhavandanā Sutta

264. Puthuddisāti bahudisā. Kā pana tāti āha “catasso disā catasso anudisā cā”ti. Anudisāgahaṇena cettha uddhaṃ adhopi gayhatīti ca dasseti. Bhūmivāsinoti bhūmipaṭibaddhavuttino. Etena rukkhapabbatanivāsinopi gahitā honti. Cirarattasamāhitacitteti upacārappanājhānāni [M 1.0341] uppādetvā aparihīnajjhānatāya cirakālaṃ samāhitacitte. Āpāṇakoṭikanti jīvitapariyantaṃ yāvajīvaṃ. Evamādīti ādi-saddena avasesapuññakiriyavatthūni saṅgaṇhāti. Niccasīlavasena pañcahi, niyamasīlavasena dasahi. Pi-saddena tato katipayehi uposathasīlavasena aṭṭhahipīti dasseti. Dhammikehīti dhammato anapetehi. Pamukhoti pamokkho.

264. "Puthuddisā" means many directions. What are they? It is said: "The four directions and the four intermediate directions." Here, by the inclusion of the intermediate directions, it is also shown that the directions above and below are included. "Bhūmivāsino" means those whose livelihood is connected to the earth. By this, those dwelling in trees and mountains are also included. "Cirarattasamāhitacitte" means in one whose mind is long concentrated through having produced access and absorption jhāna, maintaining jhāna without decline over a long time. "Āpāṇakoṭikaṃ" means until the end of life, as long as one lives. "Evamādi" includes, by the word "ādi," the remaining bases of meritorious actions. By way of constant virtue, the five precepts; by way of determined virtue, the ten precepts. The particle "pi" indicates that even a few more, such as the eight precepts of the uposatha, are also included. "Dhammikehi" means those not deviating from Dhamma. "Pamukho" means foremost.

Gahaṭṭhavandanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Gahaṭṭhavandanā Sutta is concluded.

9. Satthāravandanāsuttavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Satthāravandanā Sutta

265. Brahmajāṇukoti [V 1.0299] dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṃ pathaviyaṃ ṭhapetvā vandamāno brahmajāṇuko nāma tathābhūto hutvā. Yajitabbato yakkho, pūjanīyo. Evaṃ pūjāvisesayogato sakkoti āha “so yakkhoti so sakko”ti. Sakkassa namakkārabhājanabhūtañhi pucchanto mātali “ko nāma so yakkho”ti āha. Guṇanemittakehīti guṇahetukehi anantāni hi buddhānaṃ nāmāni, tāni ca kho sabbānipi guṇanemittakāneva. Anantaguṇattā. Vuttañhetaṃ –

265. "Brahmajāṇuko" means one who pays homage having placed the right kneecap on the ground; having become thus, he is called "brahmajāṇuko". A "yakkha" is so called because he is to be venerated (`yajitabbato`); he is worthy of worship. Thus, due to a special connection with worship, he is Sakka. It is said: "That yakkha is Sakka." Indeed, Mātali, asking about the one who was the recipient of Sakka's homage, said, "Who, indeed, is that yakkha?" "Guṇanemittakehi" means caused by qualities. For the names of the Buddhas are infinite, and all of them are indeed based on qualities, because of their infinite virtues. As it is said:

“Asaṅkhyeyyāni nāmāni, saguṇena mahesino;

Guṇena nāmamuddheyyaṃ, api nāmasahassato”ti. –

"Countless are the names of the Great Sage, due to his virtues; a name should be chosen based on virtue, even from a thousand names."

Tasmā anomanāmanti paripuṇṇaguṇanāmanti attho. Samatikkamenāti sammā samucchindanavasena atikkamanena. Kilesārīnaṃ apetacayoti apacayo, so āramitabbaṭṭhena ārāmo etesanti apacayārāmā. Tenāha “vaṭṭaviddhaṃsane ratā”ti.

Therefore, "anomanāma" means a name of complete and perfect virtue. "Samatikkamena" means by transcending, by way of rightly cutting off. "Kilesārīnaṃ apetacayo" means a waning, not an increase, of the enemies which are the defilements. They are `apacayārāmā` because they delight (`ārāma`) in this waning (`apacaya`). Hence it is said: "They delight in the destruction of the round."

Satthāravandanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Satthāravandanā Sutta is concluded.

10. Saṅghavandanāsuttavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Saṅghavandanā Sutta

266. Pūtimhi dehe mātu sarīre sayanato, attano eva vā pūtidehaṃ sarīraṃ tasmiṃ ṭhitatāya avattharitvā sayanato pūtidehasayāti [M 1.0342] yojanā. Kuṇapamheteti ete manussā asuciduggandhajegucchapaṭikkūle mātukucchisaṅkhāte kuṇapasmiṃ dasa māse nimuggā. Tesaṃ kinnāma tvaṃ pihayasīti yojanā. Etesaṃ etaṃ vihayāmīti etesaṃ isīnaṃ etaṃ sammāpaṭipattiṃ vihayāmi. Idāni taṃ paṭipattiṃ dassetuṃ “na te saṃ koṭṭhe opentī”ti vuttaṃ. Dhaññaṃ koṭṭhe na pakkhipanti pakkhipitabbassa ca abhāvato. Tenāha “na hi etesaṃ dhañña”nti. Paresaṃ niṭṭhitanti paresaṃ gahitaṃ santakaṃ tesaṃ pākāya niṭṭhitaṃ. Bhikkhācāravattenāti piṇḍācariyāya. Esamānā pariyesantā. Evaṃ pariyiṭṭhena. Yāpenti, na esanti anesanaṃ. Susamādinnasundaravatāti suṭṭhu samādinnasobhanavatā.

266. “Lying in a putrid body”: lying in the mother’s body, or lying overwhelmed in one’s own putrid body because one is situated therein—this is the construction. “From a corpse”: these people are submerged for ten months in the impure, foul-smelling, disgusting, repulsive corpse known as the mother’s womb. “For what reason do you desire them?”—this is the construction. “I emulate this of them”: I emulate this proper practice of these seers. Now, to show that practice, it is said: “They do not put into a storehouse.” They do not put grain into a storehouse, also because there is nothing to be put there. Therefore, it is said: “For they have no grain.” “Prepared by others”: what is received from others, their property, is prepared for their consumption. “By the practice of alms-gathering”: by the alms-round. “Seeking”: searching. Thus, by what has been sought. They maintain themselves; they do not seek with improper seeking. “With well-undertaken, beautiful vows”: with very well-undertaken, lovely vows.

Evaṃ subhāsitabhāsinoti ganthadhuravipassanādhurānaṃ vasena guṇaparimāṇasubhāsitasseva bhāsanasīlā[V 1.0300]. Ariyena tuṇhībhūtena tuṇhībhūtā. Tato eva manassa sātisayaṃ samañcarā. Gahitadaṇḍesu parāmāsādipayuttesu daṇḍādānādihetu uppajjanakakilesapariḷāhābhāvato nibbutā. Tenāha “vissaṭṭhadaṇḍā”ti. Sādānesūti sabhavādānesu. Anādānāti tabbirahitā. Tenāha “bhavayonī”tiādi.

“Thus, speaking what is well-spoken”: they are of the nature of speaking only what is well-spoken, in proportion to their virtue, by way of the burden of study and the burden of insight. “Silent with the noble silence”: they are silent with the silence of the noble ones. “They conducted themselves with excellence of mind.” “Among those who have taken up sticks”: among those engaged in grasping and the like, they are extinguished because of the absence of the fever of defilements that arises from the cause of taking up sticks and so forth. Therefore, it is said: “Having laid down the stick.” “Among those with grasping”: among those with grasping related to becoming. “Without grasping”: devoid of that. Therefore, it is said: “the womb of becoming,” etc.

Saṅghavandanāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Saṅghavandanā Sutta is concluded.

Dutiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Second Chapter is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

1. Chetvāsuttavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Chetvā Sutta

267. Vuttatthameva heṭṭhā devaputtasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāyaṃ.

267. The meaning has already been stated above in the commentary on the Devaputta Saṃyutta.

Chetvāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chetvā Sutta is concluded.

3. Dubbaṇṇiyasuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Dubbaṇṇiya Sutta

268. Dubbaṇṇo [M 1.0343] duddasiko virūpavaṇṇo. Okoṭimakoti rassabhāvena avarakoṭimako. Sakkena gahitanāmamevetaṃ, na pana so tathārūpo koci yakkho. Tenāha “eko rūpāvacarabrahmā”ti. Yadi evaṃ kasmā so tathārūpo hutvā āgatoti āha “sakko kirā”ti. Kathaṃ panettha ñāyati “so eko rūpāvacarabrahmā, na paneso avaruddhakayakkho”ti yuttiṃ dassento “avaruddhakayakkhā panā”tiādimāha. Devānaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā. Pharusenāti pharusasamācārena. “Ko nāma mayhaṃ āsane sannisinno”ti akkhantiṃ anuppādento khantiyaṃ ṭhatvā. Balavacittīkāranti garutaraṃ sakkārabahumānaṃ. Nīcavuttiyāti paramanipaccakāre suvūpasamane ca dassiyamāne. Sakkassa tāya eva ācārasampattiyā sakkāsane ṭhātuṃ, attano ca āvikātuṃ asakkonto antaradhāyi. Upahatacittomhīti khantimettānuddayāsabbhāvato parasmiṃ upahatacittomhīti sakko attano sabhāvaṃ vadati. Kodhavase vattetunti kodhena attano vase nibbattetuṃ na sukaromhi, atha kho kodhaṃ mayhaṃ vase na vattemīti adhippāyo. Ciraṃ na kujjhāmīti yadi me kadāci kodho uppajjeyya, taṃ kodhaṃ anuvattento cirakālaṃ na kujjhāmi[V 1.0301]. Na upanayhāmīti anto sace me kodho uppajjeyya, khippameva ca naṃ paṭivineyyanti taṃ me pubbeva vataṃ paripūritaṃ.

268. “Of ugly appearance,” ill-looking, of deformed complexion. “Okoṭimako”: he was an avarakoṭimako because of his shortness. This was merely a name assumed by him, but he was not a yakkha of such a form. Therefore, it is said: “a certain Brahmā of the form realm.” If so, why did he come in such a form? It is said: “Sakka, it is said…” But how is it known here that “he was a certain Brahmā of the form realm, and not a banished yakkha”? To show the reasoning, he said: “But banished yakkhas…” and so forth. Having heard the words of the devas. “With harshness”: with harsh conduct. “Who is it that is sitting in my seat?”: not giving rise to impatience, he remained patient. “Because of strong respect”: greater respect and honor. “With lowly conduct”: when supreme humility and complete tranquility were shown. Because of Sakka’s own perfection of conduct, he was unable to remain in Sakka’s seat or to reveal himself, and so he disappeared. “My mind is not afflicted”: Sakka speaks of his own nature, saying his mind is not afflicted towards another because of the presence of patience, loving-kindness, and compassion. “Not to act under the influence of anger”: I am not one who can be made to act under the control of anger; rather, the meaning is that I bring anger under my control. “I am not angry for long”: if anger were ever to arise in me, I would not remain angry for a long time by indulging that anger. “I do not harbor resentment”: if anger were to arise within me, I would quickly dispel it—thus that vow of mine was fulfilled beforehand.

Dubbaṇṇiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Dubbaṇṇiya Sutta is concluded.

3. Sambarimāyāsuttavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Sambarimāyā Sutta

269. Ābādhikoti ābādho assa atthīti ābādhiko. Vācesīti sikkhāpesi. Sambaro nāma asuramāyāya ādipuriso purātano asurindo. Taṃ sandhāyāha “yathā sambaro”tiādi. Evaṃ paccati aññopi māyāvī māyaṃ payojetvā. Upavādantarāyo nāma khamāpane sati vigacchati, pākatikameva hotīti āha “evamassa phāsu [M 1.0344] bhaveyyā”ti. Tenāti vepacittinā sambaravijjāya adānena vañcitattā. Tathā akatvāti isīnaṃ santikaṃ netvā khamāpanavasena kātabbaṃ akatvā.

269. “Sickly”: one who has an illness is `ābādhiko`. “He recited”: he taught. Sambara is the name of the primeval man of Asura illusion, the ancient Asura lord. Referring to him, it is said: “Just like Sambara…” and so forth. Thus another illusionist also suffers after employing illusion. The danger of blame disappears when forgiveness is asked for, and things become normal—thus it is said: “So it may be well for him.” “By him” refers to Vepacitti; because he deceived by not giving Sambara’s knowledge. “Not having done so”: not having done what should be done, which is to take them to the sages and ask for forgiveness.

Sambarimāyāsuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Sambarimāyā Sutta is concluded.

4. Accayasuttavaṇṇanā

4. Commentary on the Accaya Sutta

270. Sampayojesunti aññamaññaṃ vācasikaṃ pharusaṃ payojesuṃ. Tenāha “kalahaṃ akaṃsū”ti, vivādaṃ akaṃsūti attho. Atikkammavacananti vacīsaṃvaraṃ atikkamitvā vacanaṃ. Yasmā accaye desiyamāne taṃ khīṇayati aññamaññassa khamamānassa khamanaṃ paṭiggaṇhato, tasmā vuttaṃ “nappaṭigaṇhātīti na khamatī”ti. Tumhākaṃ vase vattatu, visevitaṃ akatvā yathākāmakaraṇīyo hotu. Mittadhammo idha uttarapadalopena “mitto”ti vuttoti āha “mittadhamme”ti. Karaṇavacananti “mittehī”ti karaṇavacanaṃ bhummatthe. Tenāha “mittesū”ti. Yathā nibbattasabhāvassa bhāvato aññathattaṃ jarā, evaṃ mittabhāvato vuttavipariyāyo amittadhammo jarāpariyāyena vutto. Agārayhaṃ anavajjaṃ sabbaso pahīnakilesaṃ. Tenāha “khīṇāsavapuggala”nti.

270. “They stirred each other up”: they used harsh verbal exchanges with each other. Therefore, it is said: “they engaged in quarrels,” meaning they engaged in disputes. “Transgressing speech”: speech that transgresses verbal restraint. Because when a transgression is confessed, it is worn away for one who forgives another and accepts that forgiveness; therefore, it is said: “does not accept” means “does not forgive.” “Let it remain under your control”: meaning without having been ill-served, let him be able to do as he wishes. Here, the term “mitta” (friend) is used by eliding the latter part of the compound, thus it is said: “in friendly qualities.” “Karaṇavacana” (instrumental case): the instrumental case “by friends” is used in the sense of the locative. Therefore, it is said: “among friends.” Just as aging is the alteration from the state of one who is born, so too the stated opposite of friendly qualities, unfriendly qualities, are described in terms of aging. “Blameless and irreproachable”: one who has entirely abandoned defilements. Therefore, it is said: “a person whose taints are destroyed.”

Accayasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Accaya Sutta is concluded.

5. Akkodhasuttavaṇṇanā

5. Commentary on the Akkodha Sutta

271. Kodho tumhe mā abhibhavīti ettha kodhena anabhibhavanīyattaṃ khantimettākaruṇāditappaṭipakkhadhammaparibrūhanena[V 1.0302]. Tathā hi taṃsamaṅgino kodho abhibhuyyatīti āha “tumheva kodhaṃ abhibhavatha. Kujjhantānaṃ mā paṭikujjhitthā”ti. Paṭipadāti esā paṭipatti. Mettāti appanāppattā mettā. Tadupacāro mettāpubbabhāgo. Na vihiṃsati kiñci etāyāti avihiṃsā. Karuṇāti appanāppattakaruṇā veditabbā. Tadupacāro [M 1.0345] karuṇāpubbabhāgo. Lāmakajananti khantiādīsu yonisomanasikārābhāvena gārayhasamācārasamāyogena ca nihīnaṃ janaṃ. Paccayaparisuddhiyā kodho abhimaddamāno puggalaṃ abhimaddati, tassa so paṭisaṅkhānabhāvanābalehi sammadeva pahātabboti.

271. Herein, not being overpowered by anger is achieved through the cultivation of opposing qualities such as patience, loving-kindness, compassion, and so forth. Indeed, for one endowed with such qualities, anger is overcome. Thus it is said: “You should overcome anger. Do not retaliate against those who are angry.” “The practice” means this very practice. “Loving-kindness” is loving-kindness that has attained absorption. Its access is the preliminary stage of loving-kindness. “Non-harming” means that one does not harm anything by it. “Compassion” should be understood as compassion that has attained absorption. Its access is the preliminary stage of compassion. “Inferior people” means lowly people due to the absence of wise attention regarding patience and so forth, and due to association with blameworthy conduct. Anger, while crushing a person, assails the purity of their requisites; therefore, it should be rightly abandoned through the power of reflection and development.

Akkodhasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Akkodha Sutta is concluded.

Tatiyavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Third Chapter is concluded.

Sāratthappakāsiniyā saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya

The Sāratthappakāsinī, the Commentary on the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Sakkasaṃyuttavaṇṇanāya līnatthappakāsanā samattā.

The Līnatthappakāsanā on the Commentary to the Sakka Saṃyutta is concluded.

Niṭṭhitā ca sāratthappakāsiniyā

And the Sāratthappakāsinī is concluded.

Saṃyuttanikāya-aṭṭhakathāya sagāthāvaggavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Sagāthāvagga of the Commentary to the Saṃyutta Nikāya.

Paṭhamo bhāgo niṭṭhito.

The First Part is concluded.
